articles.title: Scotland: What does Sebastien Pocognoli do about Ben Gannon-Doak?
articles.summary: As Scotland prepare to conclude their Nations League group campaign in Switzerland, there are concerns about how new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli is utilising one of his most exciting assets.
articles.body:
Two years ago, when Scotland defeated Croatia in the Nations League, that November night at Hampden was the dawn of Ben Gannon-Doak .

The then-teenager took £77m Manchester City man Josko Gvardiol to the cleaners and fans demanded the national team be built around the winger.

The Tartan Army's love for him has never faded - it arguably peaked when he stole the show in Scotland's World Cup opening win over Haiti - but it is fair to say they are growing frustrated, arguably on the Bournemouth man's behalf.

Under Sebastien Pocognoli, Gannon-Doak - who turned 21 on Wednesday - has been deployed at right wing-back, a role that demands defensive instincts unnatural to the pacy attacker.

It is already clear the new head coach is wedded to his preferred system, but it is one that is stifling one of Scotland's greatest attacking outlets - even though his final product still leaves a lot to be desired.

As his side prepare to visit Nations League Group B1 leaders Switzerland on Monday needing a win to have any chance of a promotion play-off place, Pocognoli has addressed both concerns - citing he is not uneasy about either - but pundits and punters alike cannot seem to shift their suspicions.

In that 1-0 victory over 10-man Croatia, it was Gannon-Doak's fearlessness in facing one of Europe's most elite and experienced teams that caught the eye.

His electric speed and directness excited a support who had long been crying out for a player with such qualities and the confidence in applying them. A natural winger, if you will.

In Pocognoli's system, though, there is no space for wingers. Something that former Rangers full-back Richard Foster says must "scunner" the wee man.

"When you're a full-back and you get to play wing-back, it's amazing - all of a sudden you are 10-20 yards up the pitch, doing more attacking and you can be a bit more aggressive," he said on BBC Scotland's Sportsound.

"When you ask a winger to do that, most of the time they are absolutely scunnered. They are thinking 'I don't want to go back there'.

Why 'inspiring' Van Gaal influences Scotland head coach Pocognoli

Six goals to go - will McGinn catch Dalglish & Law?

"Looking at the squad [against North Macedonia], the three most exciting players we had - Findlay Curtis, Josh McPake and Gannon-Doak - are all wingers and he didn't bring two on.

"You look at the previous game [against Slovenia] and the difference McPake and Curtis made by coming on and taking players on - it gives everyone a lift.

"As a fan, you want to get excited about what you are watching. We are playing in a shape where we have the most exciting talents on the bench and they can't get on unless you adjust things. I just think he has to change the formation."

Foster is far from the only one wishing for a shift in shape - and not just for Gannon-Doak's benefit. Much has been made about the Scots' options in defence , too, and whether they match-up to the method.

However, it is arguable Gannon-Doak is the biggest casualty of them all.

"I don't think we're getting the best out of Ben," former Scotland captain Scott Brown told BBC Scotland.

"You saw him making so many last-ditch headers on Friday. He's having to add things to his game that he probably hasn't done before, like throw-ins, defending one-v-one."

No need to mention that throw-in, Scott. But that wasn't the only instance where Gannon-Doak looked a little lost. Think the 'Confused Travolta' meme.

Pocognoli 'happy' despite Gannon-Doak flaws

While his position is a new worry, his precision with his final product is not.

Almost in a microcosm, Gannon-Doak's play was laid bare when be hurtled to the byeline before winning what turned out to be the match-winning penalty against the North Macedonians on Friday.

"He made a great run for the penalty, but I did think he could have got his shot away a bit earlier and maybe not taken that extra touch," Brown said.

Back in 2024, the wee live-wire was forgiven for not always finding a pal with a pass or choking at crunch time with his final ball.

However, as the years go on and the caps rack up, his shortcomings are still on show. His end product is still largely poor and patience is wearing thin.

"As long as he is high on the pitch and is creating one-v-ones, I am happy," Pocognoli reiterated post his maiden Hampden win.

"With Ben, we know that he is a young age and needs to work on specific things. On Friday night, he had great opportunities.

"We know that he needs to improve on the end product. But he created a penalty and, against Slovenia and North Macedonia away, he created a number of unbelievable one-v-ones. He did that on Friday night as well.

"We know he can be good if we dominate the game and he can get in good positions if we control the ball.

So Pocognoli is comfortable for now. Already that appears to be a running theme for the head coach - even if others are not.

articles.title: Homophobia in football: Reports of abuse on the rise in English football
articles.summary: Homophobia and transphobia are on the rise in English football, with new data revealing record numbers of discrimination reports in the game - so what is the Premier League doing about it?
articles.body:
Warning: this article contains offensive language

Homophobia and transphobia are on the rise in English football, with new data revealing record numbers of discrimination reports in the game - so what is the Premier League doing about it?

Last season, with little fanfare, the league introduced a new LGBTQ+ celebratory activation in February, Premier League With Pride.

The lowkey launch contrasts with the landscape of a few years ago, when England internationals like Jordan Henderson and Conor Coady were proudly proclaiming their allyship.

"The one thing it [Premier League With Pride last season] was lacking was engagement from players," said Jon Holmes, founder and lead of news organisation and campaign group Sports Media LGBT+.

"Not only would you have the rainbow armbands, but clearer allyship from players - that was more around the late 2010s. That has been in decline."

A report last month from anti-discrimination charity Kick It Out says they received a new high of 1,744 discrimination reports during the 2025-26 season, a 25% increase on the previous campaign. In this, reports of homophobia rose 46% to 203.

Kick It Out said it had received 142 reports of discriminatory mass chanting during the season, a 41% increase on 2024-25 and the highest number recorded. These reports included increases in homophobic and transphobic chants.

A prime example is the 'rent boy' chant predominantly aimed at Chelsea players and fans, for which incidents had dropped since it was criminalised in 2022. However, the combined 24 reports of homophobic chanting in 2025-26 season were the most in three years.

According to Kick It Out, , external many of the incidents over the past few seasons can be linked to domestic and world events, such as the Supreme Court ruling on gender leading to the FA's ban on transgender women in the women's game, which it says led to a spike in transphobic abuse.

How inclusive is your Premier League club?

BBC Sport asked all 20 Premier League clubs what diversity policies they have regarding the LGBTQ+ community, and how much of their budget is dedicated to such schemes.

Nine clubs responded to the BBC request. None said how much money they invest in these areas.

A Nottingham Forest spokesperson told BBC Sport: "The club commits significant funding to this important area, and has an Equality, Diversity and Inclusion lead whose role is dedicated to ensuring inclusion is at the heart of everything we do."

Some clubs do visibly engage with their local LGBTQ+ community. Leeds United have been a sponsor of the city's Pride celebrations since 2018. Luke Ayling, then Leeds captain, marched in the Pride parade in 2022.

Liverpool and Brighton are annually represented in their city's extensive Pride events, as are the Manchester clubs.

Manchester City host an annual Progress flag-raising ceremony, while Manchester United said staff marched in the city centre parade. They also ran a flag competition with LGBTQ+ supporters' club Rainbow Devils, with the winning design displayed at Old Trafford for all matchdays.

Tottenham said that at the start of 2024, Spurs in the Community helped launch a weekly football session for members of the LGBTQ+ community.

And for the first time this season, all 20 current Premier League clubs have dedicated fan groups for LGBTQ+ supporters.

"It feels like there is a renaissance in the LGBT fan movement," said Holmes. "There is a rise in homophobia, but it does seem like the authorities are sitting up and taking notice. We can feel a degree of optimism."

But it is difficult for Premier League teams to encourage LGBTQ+ allyship and diversity, when representation within clubs is a mixed bag at best.

According to Kick It Out, which gathered data on the senior management teams from 17 out of the 20 current Premier League clubs, just 0.3% of people in those roles openly identify as LGBTQ+ - well below the UK population average according to latest national census data, with 4% of the British population identifying as LGBTQ+.

At a senior coaching level, from 11 clubs which responded there is no-one from the LGBTQ+ community.

Kick It Out says, comparing the dataset to relevant census data, that if football's workforce was truly representative of local communities, over 100 more people from the LGBTQ+ community would have to be employed at Premier League clubs.

The Premier League previously had a high profile association with LGBTQ+ charity Stonewall's Rainbow Laces campaign - but this was ended before the 2025-26 season

Rainbow Laces started in 2014-15 as a collaboration between Stonewall, Paddy Power and the Premier League. For two game weeks, usually around the end of November, players would wear rainbow-coloured laces or armbands, and the colourful branding would be seen in grounds and on broadcast idents.

Holmes said by the end it was doing more harm than good.

"I think the novelty of Rainbow Laces wore off," he told BBC Sport. "It also became more newsworthy to talk about the controversies; it became more difficult for players to engage without difficult questions.

"Also, club media departments are more risk averse, given growing toxicity on social media.

"It has been misconstrued that players were forced to engage, I think it was because Rainbow Laces became de rigueur, and it was perceived that captains would need to lead with the armband and allyship."

Rainbow armbands were introduced in 2017 for captains, having first been worn by MLS club Orlando City following the mass shooting at Pulse, an LGBTQ+ nightclub, in the city in 2016.

But the Premier League held its final Rainbow Laces campaign from 29 November to 5 December, 2024, and it was surrounded by controversy.

Marc Guehi, then Crystal Palace captain, wrote 'I Love Jesus' on his armband in what was widely viewed as a protest against wearing the armband (which was not mandatory).

Ipswich captain Sam Morsy refused to wear the armband, while Manchester United scrapped plans for a Rainbow Laces-themed jacket during the pre-match ceremonies following an objection by Noussair Mazraoui.

Simon Blake, CEO of Stonewall, admitted to BBC Sport that by the end of its 12-year lifespan in the Premier League, Rainbow Laces in that form had run its course.

"When it started, getting a few people to wear the laces was success," he said. "When it ended, when a few people didn't wear them there was criticism.

"If a campaign no longer has a positive vibe, perhaps it is time to do something different.

"Everything must evolve and change, but visibility still matters, it is important not to throw the baby out with the bathwater."

Stonewall held its first ever Rainbow Laces Day on 8 October this year, to encourage LGBTQ+ people to engage with sport. It had no connection with the Premier League.

Is the religion of players having an impact?

It is notable that the players most ardently against Rainbow Laces were also vocal in their religious beliefs.

Guehi has spoken of the importance in his life of his faith and was one of several devout Christian players in the Crystal Palace dressing room. Both Morsy and Mazraoui are practicing Muslims.

Both Holmes and Blake acknowledge that this may have had an impact on Rainbow Laces.

"The influence of religion is clearly quite significant, but I think more understanding is coming in too," said Holmes.

"We have seen many parts of life less willing to engage with Pride, and football reflects that. The nature of LGBT campaigns is peaks and troughs, and we are in a trough."

"We don't have any specific data about what people's beliefs and views are, but we are in a world where people have different views, even within religions themselves," added Blake.

"The important thing is about behaviours, and we must learn to live with people who have these different beliefs and respect them.

"I don't want to speculate, as it would be too easy to assume people of faith would not be inclusive, I know from my work across 30 years that is not true; I have worked with many religious people who are LGBTQ+ supportive. Freedom of belief is important."

'Previously unacceptable views are now being expressed freely'

The current picture is a difficult one for gay and trans people in football at all levels.

The grassroots game is where the bulk of the increase in abuse has occurred, says Kick It Out, which claims it received 140% more reports last year than in the 2024-25 season. Three quarters of these reports are from senior grassroots games, where the players are over 18.

Away from football, research by Stonewall published in October found 11% of LGBTQ+ people in the UK avoid the gym, exercise classes or sports groups for fear of discrimination. Among trans people, the figure rises to 29%.

It said 15% of LGBTQ+ people who had been to a live sporting event, or watched sport in a bar, in the past year had experienced discrimination there. This rose to 26% for trans people.

"What we know is that there is a lot of work going on around equality and diversity; we also know homophobia and transphobia continue to be rife," Blake said.

"We are in a world, whether at Premier League or grassroots football, where views that may have been perceived to be unacceptable are now being expressed freely. That influences peoples' relationship with sport."

Premier League With Pride will return in 2026-27.

"The matchday activations take place in February in line with LGBTQ+ History Month, when the league and clubs will showcase their commitment to LGBTQ+ inclusion," a Premier League spokesperson told BBC Sport.

"There will be two match rounds dedicated to Premier League With Pride. This means all 20 clubs have a home game during that period, providing an opportunity to highlight and celebrate the LGBTQ+ community in football and showcase the work undertaken to make the game more inclusive.

"There is no centralised activation lined up for November."

articles.title: Andy Burnham urges caution on lifting Saturday 3pm TV blackout in UK
articles.summary: Andy Burnham urges caution on lifting the Saturday 3pm TV blackout in the UK, saying the health of the football pyramid should come first.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has urged caution on lifting the Saturday 3pm TV blackout in the UK, saying the health of the football pyramid should come first.

The rule was introduced in the 1960s to encourage fans to attend lower league games and prevents matches from being shown on UK television between 2:45pm and 5:15pm on Saturdays.

The blackout, which is enforced by Article 48 of the Uefa Statutes and is imposed by the English and Scottish football associations, comes into effect when 50% of fixtures in the top two divisions are scheduled to kick off at 3pm.

The Premier League is in the middle of a record £6.7bn domestic TV deal for Sky and TNT to show up to 270 live games a season.

But there could be room for change with the 3pm rule in the upcoming broadcast cycle, as the rights deals for the Premier League, EFL and SPFL all end in 2028-29.

The prime minister said any decision to remove the ban would require careful thought about the consequences.

"I would urge a bit of caution [on the blackout], because it does protect the income of lower-league clubs," Burnham said.

Scottish football could pave way for 3pm TV blackout to end

Why does football have Saturday 3pm TV blackout in UK?

"If you have effectively wall-to-wall Premier League football at any time, it takes away perhaps the incentive to go and watch the football league or non-league.

"So I think it has to be considered carefully. I'm not going to take the pure consumer view here. I'll take the health-of-football approach to this particular issue."

Only the FA Cup final, which traditionally kicks off at 3pm, is allowed to be broadcast during the blackout window.

In October, the SPFL said it is "flexible about the number of games" that will form part of the TV new deal, which BBC Sport understands includes matches shown on a Saturday afternoon.

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters has previously said a decision about whether the blackout stays in place would need to be made in the future.

But Burnham added: "I would first of all want to protect the football pyramid before I agree to saying 'let's have even more live football'".

"I think it's about protecting the experience with the paying supporter, protecting the football pyramid. Those issues matter to me, first of all."

articles.title: Bundesliga: así se arma un negocio de 590 millones por ‘matchday’
articles.standfirst: El fútbol profesional alemán reunió a 21,4 millones de espectadores en las gradas de Primera y Segunda División la pasada temporada
articles.summary: El fútbol profesional alemán reunió a 21,4 millones de espectadores en las gradas de Primera y Segunda División la pasada temporada
articles.body: La Bundesliga tiene en sus gradas a su mayor aliado. La liga alemana cerró la última temporada con 21,4 millones aficionados que vieron in situ sus partidos, incluyendo los 36 clubes de Primera y Segunda División. La media es de 34.974 espectadores, aunque el equipo con mayor asistencia a su estadio, el Borussia Dortmund, dobla esta cifra, según datos recabados por la propia competición y a los que ha tenido acceso Intelligence 2P, la unidad de estrategia e inteligencia de mercado de 2Playbook. Una fidelidad que se traduce en cientos de millones de euros de facturación directa por matchday, pero que también explica el por qué de la elevada inversión de compañías locales en patrocinio. Con estas cifras de ocupación, y a una media de 27,5 euros de valor de la entrada, el ticketing generó un total de 590 millones de euros en 2025-2026. En la Primera División alemana se vendieron 12,7 millones de entradas –incluidos abonos–, lo que supone un 9,1% más respecto a la temporada anterior. La máxima categoría registró una asistencia media de 41.562 espectadores por partido, 3.500 más asistentes a cada partido respecto a 2024-2025. En este incremento, una de las claves fue la vuelta a la élite del FC Köln y del Hamburgo, dos de los clubes con mayor masa social y que registran mejores datos de asistencia. Sus campos tienen más de 50.000 asientos, con lo que ello implica en una liga que registra sold outs en casi todos sus partidos. De hecho, la propia liga reconoce el impacto del cambio de categoría de estos dos clubes para justificar el descenso del 7% que registró la asistencia en la Bundesliga 2: 8,7 millones en total, y una media de 28.386 espectadores por partido. De los 80.000 en Dortmund a los 46.000 del Kaiserslautern Por clubes, el Signal Iduna Park de Dortmund continúa reinando en la asistencia, con 80.000 espectadores en cada partido. El campo pone el cartel de no hay billetes en cada evento y se beneficia de gradas como el Muro Amarillo, donde 25.000 aficionados ven los encuentros de pie. En esa zona alta le sigue el Allianz Arena del FC Bayern, con cerca de 75.000 asistentes en cada partido del equipo de Múnich, y cierra el podio el recién ascendido Hamburgo, un histórico del fútbol germano y que recibió a 56.900 espectadores, de media, a su estadio cada quince días. En términos de negocio, esta fidelidad de las aficiones se traduce en mucho dinero. El Dortmund ya ha consolidado una facturación superior a 50 millones de euros por matchplay según datos de Intelligence 2P. De media, los equipos de la Bundesliga facturan 33,3 millones de euros anuales por día de partido, con una horquilla que va de los 13,1 millones entre los equipos de la zona baja, hasta los 54,4 millones de euros de los clubes clasificados para Europa. Por su parte, en Segunda División, otro clásico como el Schalke 04 registró las cifras de asistencia más altas, con más de 61.000 espectadores por partido, por delante del Hertha de Berlín, con más de 47.000, y del FC Kaiserslautern, con casi 46.000 espectadores, de media. Cifras que ubicaría a todos ellos, incluyendo los de Bundesliga 2, a niveles de los estadios con más asistencia de LaLiga. En esta categoría, los equipos facturaron una media de 15,2 millones de euros por matchday, con una horquilla que en la zona baja es igual a Primera División (13,1 millones), pero que mengua notablemente en la comparativa entre los clubes de la zona alta: 17,4 millones de euros, un 68% por debajo de los grandes de Alemania. Además de grandes estadios y una población mucho mayor que la de España –83,6 millones de habitantes–, un elemento clave para entender los elevados ingresos por taquilla es que cuentan con aficiones que no fallan ningún fin de semana: 16 de los 18 clubes de Bundesliga superaron el 90% de ocupación en toda la temporada. ¿Cuánto vale una entrada en Bundesliga? El precio medio de una entrada para un partido de la Bundesliga (Primera División), incluyendo el IVA y el coste del transporte público, fue de 30,77 euros, un 6,9% más interanual. En Bundesliga 2, la entrada tenía un valor medio de 24,34 euros, un 1,5% por debajo de lo que costaba en 2024-2025. Además, el informe de la DFL, gestora de la competición, desgrana las entradas de partido y los abonos. Los carnés de temporada suponen un 56% de los tickets, con más de 12 millones de abonados en 2025-2026. De estos, 7,1 millones correspondieron a clubes de Primera División, por los 4,9 millones de Bundesliga 2. El 43,88% restante se comercializaron con entradas eventuales, con 5,7 millones en Primera y 3,7 millones en Segunda, para un total de casi 9,4 millones de tickets de partido. Cabe destacar que fue mayor el porcentaje de abonos vendidos, sobre las entradas totales, en Bundesliga 2 que en la máxima categoría.

articles.title: How Serie A's Monza are aiming to gatecrash a crowded market
articles.summary: How Serie A outfit Monza are trying to make an impact in the shadow Milan giants and fashionable Como.
articles.body:
Think Monza, and the mind conjures up famous winning drives by Lewis Hamilton and Michael Schumacher, and by Kimi Antonelli this year on the way to his first Formula 1 title.

Sporting theatre on four wheels is not all that this northern Italian city has to offer, though.

Just under four miles from the historic home of motor racing's Italian Grand Prix sits the 17,000-capacity Stadio Brianteo, home to Serie A football club AC Monza.

It's not easy for the club to capture attention, given European giants AC Milan and Inter Milan play at the San Siro, a 20-minute drive away, while the romantic lure of Como is less than an hour from here by train.

But Monza have their own captivating story to tell.

Founded in 1912, the Biancorossi - white and reds - did not even play in Serie B for the first time until 1951. As recently as 2017, they were playing part-time in Serie D.

Under the guidance of former player Giovanni Stroppa, Monza were promoted to Serie A for the first time in 2022. Stroppa was sacked after a slow start in the top flight, but Monza survived for three years before being relegated.

They then bounced back immediately, earning their place among the elite again in May of this year.

Now owned by American venture capitalists Beckett Layne Ventures (BLV), and with former Southampton boss Ivan Juric in the manager's chair, Monza have a clear vision for how they can make an impact in their crowded geographical market.

I am speaking to Monza chief executive Mauro Baldissoni in an office at the Stadio Brianteo, having been given a brief tour of the club's training facilities at Monzello, less than a five-minute drive away.

The atmosphere is positive after a 4-0 win over Cagliari the previous night - the club's biggest ever Serie A victory.

Monza sit third bottom at the time of writing, a point from safety, but the club feel so much is in their favour.

"First off, Monza is on the outskirts of Milan, so the location is attractive for the players," says Baldissoni. "It's a good point of visibility for what we do.

"There is a point of attraction and point of awareness about Monza, because it is already known in the world for luxury sports through the association with Formula 1.

"The infrastructure at the club is larger and probably more efficient than Milanello, the sporting centre of Milan, because they cannot have all the teams from the youngest in the academy to the first team like we can. This province specifically is one of the richest in terms of GDP in Europe.

"So, you have all the premises to create a good project. And there is always people coming to watch.

"Yesterday there were people from Newcastle, Fulham, Southampton, Sunderland, Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund at the game, and there were others. If you come here, you can watch AC Milan, Como, [an] Atalanta game, Inter game, and Monza.

"Scouts and sporting directors can come for two days and watch different games at a high level."

Monza president Lauren Crampsie was previously the chief marketing officer at Chelsea.

She is now of the founders of BLV, which paid €45m to the family of the late Silvio Berlusconi to buy up Monza.

Crampsie, 46, watched the pre-match build-up from the pitch before the Cagliari win, making sure all the details were in order. Afterwards, she is mindful to let the players and coaching staff enjoy their victory.

Young striker Gustavo Varela is the star of the night, scoring two of his 11 goals in all competitions so far this season, earning himself a first senior call-up to the Portugal squad.

Monza paid Benfica £2.5m for the 21-year-old, who is currently top scorer in Serie A, with nine in nine games.

Already there are big-name suitors sniffing around, doubtless willing to pay a fee significantly higher than the one Monza forked out.

It is a perfect illustration of the business model the club are trying to create.

"We always think the club's mission is to win games, but it is also about forming players that are part of their academy first and also trying to identify talents that can fit with the purposes and the style of the club," says Baldissoni, who spent 10 years with Roma before leaving in 2020.

"In Rome we were able to identify young talents like Marquinhos, who was 18 years old and able to play as a starter before we sold him to Paris St-Germain.

"There were others like Erik Lamela and Mo Salah. But in Rome it is more difficult because expectations are higher.

"In Monza the idea is the same. The pressure is bigger because the impact of relegation on revenues is worse. But the environment and the sporting expectations are more manageable for a young player who has more time to form his emotional background."

Monza fought off competition from League One club Leicester to sign Southampton's England youth international Jay Robinson on loan this season, with Juric's presence being key.

The 19-year-old has already played 10 times in all competitions, scoring twice.

Fiorentina, Roma, Como and Juventus provide a stiff run of fixtures for Monza heading towards Christmas, before an equally important match against Venezia, who are currently one place and one point worse off in the table.

Baldissoni is optimistic. His wider view of the football landscape is not altered by the knowledge that promoted Premier League trio Coventry, Hull and Ipswich all spent in excess of £120m in the summer, a figure Monza can only dream of.

Plans are under way to refurbish Stadio Brianteo, which has covering over a single stand.

"Infrastructure is the weakest point in Italy under the competition point of view, to compete with other global markets," Baldissoni says.

"But there are costs and there are investments."

He says the stadium is "an investment meant to generate more revenues".

"Of course, the Premier League's revenues are much higher than all the other leagues, so those clubs have a competitive advantage.

"But they also overpay players because it's Premier League. Maybe they get a player that I would like to have because they can pay more, but maybe I can find another player that is not that far away. Then you have to be able to form the player.

"So, you identify a talent early, and then you keep forming him to bring him to a level where some other players already are. Maybe then we sell him to Premier League?"

It's a delicate balancing act, but Monza are sure it can be done.

"Sassuolo made it to Serie A 13 years ago for the first time and until last season, spent all that time in Serie A. Atalanta was going up and down and now it's one of the prominent teams, targeting European competitions every year," Baldissoni says.

"This is out of the work they've been doing in terms of identifying talents, forming talents, and remaining competitive.

"That is the target. It is possible. Let's see if we can make it."

articles.title: Sanitas entrega al Real Madrid Femenino sus nuevas tarjetas sanitarias digitales
articles.standfirst: Las futbolistas podrán acceder a la red médica de Sanitas y utilizar Blua para hacer videoconsultas, consultar informes clínicos y seguir indicadores de salud
articles.summary: Las futbolistas podrán acceder a la red médica de Sanitas y utilizar Blua para hacer videoconsultas, consultar informes clínicos y seguir indicadores de salud
articles.body: Las jugadoras del primer equipo femenino del Real Madrid ya tienen sus nuevas tarjetas sanitarias digitales. Sanitas, proveedor médico oficial del club, se las entregó en un acto en la Ciudad Deportiva del Real Madrid al que asistieron Pau Quesada, entrenador del equipo, y Javier Gabás, director general de Sanitas Mayores. Las tarjetas dan acceso a la red asistencial de Sanitas y a los servicios digitales de Blua. Desde la plataforma, las futbolistas pueden hacer videoconsultas, consultar sus informes clínicos y seguir determinados indicadores de salud sin desplazarse. “Para Sanitas es una satisfacción seguir acompañando a un equipo que es ejemplo de esfuerzo y superación. Las jugadoras del Real Madrid demuestran cada día la importancia de la preparación física y del cuidado de la salud para afrontar las exigencias de la competición. Contribuir a su bienestar y rendimiento deportivo a través de nuestros profesionales y servicios médicos es una parte fundamental de nuestra colaboración con el club”, explicó Gabás. El acuerdo abarca a los primeros equipos masculino y femenino de fútbol y al de baloncesto. Sanitas pone a su disposición una red de profesionales sanitarios, centros especializados y servicios médicos de alta complejidad, además de herramientas digitales para el seguimiento de la salud de los deportistas. Las revisiones y pruebas médicas de los jugadores y jugadoras del club se realizan en el Hospital Blua Sanitas Valdebebas, el primer hospital nativo digital de España, según la compañía. El centro incorpora tecnología de última generación y un modelo asistencial orientado a mejorar la experiencia del paciente.

articles.title: España hace autocrítica: "No hay excusas, no nos gusta perder"
articles.standfirst: El vestuario asume los errores, pero mira al futuro con optimismo.
articles.summary: El vestuario asume los errores, pero mira al futuro con optimismo.
articles.body: Se acabó la racha. A España le tocó perder. Algo lógico en el fútbol, pero inusual para el equipo de Luis de la Fuente. Han tenido que pasar 43 partidos para que una derrota interrumpiese una racha que ya es historia del fútbol mundial. "Creo que nos ha faltado un poco de intensidad en el primer tiempo, un poco de ideas en el juego. También es verdad que ha sido una semana un poco peculiar, no quiero decir que sea una excusa porque no, una selección como nosotros no tenemos que tener excusas, pero ha sido un poco peculiar" aseguró Laporte. En el vestuario se hace autocrítica. Hay aspectos que mejorar, asignaturas pendientes. Pero sin volverse locos. Perder de vez en cuando es lógico y hacerlo contra la número 4 del mundo, que para Unai Simón podría ser perfectamente la número 2, todavía más: "Siempre duele perder. Sabíamos que en algún momento se iba a acabar la racha. Inglaterra es una selección con la que podía darse el caso porque en mi opinión creo que es la segunda mejor selección del mundo, aunque el ranking FIFA no lo diga, creo que el nivel que tienen es comparable al nuestro. Duele por perder. Pero lo bueno es que perder aquí te da chance de poder seguir en cuartos de final. De corregir muchos errores y que en marzo no vuelva a pasar", aseguraba el recientemente reconocido como mejor portero del mundo. Ser primeros de grupo era un objetivo claro, pero el escenario ahora no cambia. España está en cuartos, a dos partidos de otra Final Four y a sólo cuatro de otro título continental. "Nosotros siempre queremos ganar. Queríamos ser primeros porque es importante para nosotros. Y más después del del Mundial que hemos hecho. Somos los número uno actualmente y queríamos demostrarlo hoy también", lamentaba Laporte. Muchas veces las derrotas te ayudan a valorar todo lo que has conseguido antes. Quizá este sea uno de esos casos. Lo es, al menos, para De la Fuente: "Hemos vivido una semana peculiar, con exigencias máximas, pero el equipo ha dado la cara en todo momento. Lo que hace esta derrota es poner aún más en valor todo lo que hemos conseguido hasta ahora. No se puede ganar siempre, por mucho que hayamos puesto el listón muy alto con tres años sin perder y levantando títulos. El espíritu, la ambición y la confianza en este grupo siguen intactos de cara a lo que viene en marzo. El privilegio, insisto, es tener a todas estas futbolistas maravillosas que nos han traído hasta donde nos han traído hasta ahora, y todavía, insisto, hay muchas cosas por hacer", explicó el técnico. Pese a todo, el vestuario despide el año que todos soñaban con los deberes hechos: la segunda estrella ya está bordada en el pecho de los campeones del mundo y el billete para cuartos de final de la Nations League, en plena Semana Santa de 2027, comprado. La ida será en Mestalla; la vuelta, veremos dónde y contra quién.

articles.title: Lucy Bronze leads Chelsea to biggest WSL win of season over Man City as Mary Earps gives Arsenal another headache at home
articles.summary: Digital journalist Laura Hunter returns for a second season with a WSL-dedicated column, analysing all the big talking points from across the weekend's action; this week's focus is on the heroic performances of two England legends Lucy Bronze and Mary Earps
articles.body:
Nothing makes Lucy Bronze prouder than a clean sheet. She absolutely thrives off the scrap and skirmish of it. Against Manchester City, her determination to put defensive duty above all else won Chelsea a priceless three points.

Not since November 2025 had the WSL's leading scorer Khadija Shaw failed to register a shot on target in a game. Bronze can pocket that achievement. She had help from other members of the backline - Veerle Buurman was standout too - but Chelsea's captain led the lockdown.

Shaw was isolated, limited in time and space, and restricted in her movement. "We had to be like dogs in this game," Bronze told BBC Sport afterwards. "We were very focused on that." They shackled Shaw in a way few defences across Europe are able to, Bronze acting as the technical and tactical lynchpin.

This, Chelsea's biggest win of the season so far, is one that sees them leapfrog their greatest rivals in the race for this year's title. It will be a campaign built on solidity as much as anything else. The Blues have given up a miserly 0.5 goals per 90 so far.

Sonia Bompastor had stressed the importance of winning duels pre-game and that emphasis ran through the spine of her team. She made a point of praising Bronze's leadership in the handling of City's threats post-match, capping a heroic display with a game-high 13 defensive contributions.

Collectively, Chelsea won the duel count 47-37 and were equally better in possession, with more systematic and sustained pressure in the opposition half. Bronze won that contest too. No Chelsea player created more chances (2) or completed more final third passes (9) than her. She also registered more touches than any team-mate (87).

Meanwhile, Shaw was reduced to taking 45 per cent of her open play touches in City's defensive half and received more passes from goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita (6) than any outfield player. City's usual rhythm was heavily disrupted and meant the striker blanked in a league game for the first time this season.

Even in the second half, when Andree Jeglertz adjusted his setup to bring Vivianne Miedema into the pocket behind Shaw, Chelsea adapted to match up. Bronze smelt the danger, commanding others to follow her exemplary lead.

A situation in the 75th minute summed up Chelsea's application perfectly.

The ball is punched through the lines to Shaw, usually so reliable in her hold-up play. But on this occasion Buurman is encouraged to engage aggressively and the ball turns over. Aggie Beever-Jones and Maika Hamano exchange passes on halfway, before the latter opts to go long in search of Alyssa Thompson's far side run.

The sequence of events that follow spell the beginning of the end for City. Yamashita feels compelled to try and cut out the pass but is caught in no man's land, mistiming her intervention and gets sent off for denying Thompson a goalscoring opportunity. If City were struggling to get at Chelsea with 11, playing with 10 made the task impossible.

Bompastor got her tactical approach spot on at Stamford Bridge, balancing enough risk with sensible stability. But she was reliant on perfect execution of the game plan from her players. They delivered. None more so than evergreen Bronze.

Another to confess to "love defending" at the weekend was Mary Earps.

Her heroism in defending London City's goal at the Emirates earned her side a valiant point against Arsenal as they continue to hold on to third spot while also staying in touch with the top two. "This game sums up why I wanted to come back and play in the best league in the world," she told Sky Sports afterwards.

England fans will have fond memories of Earps in this vein, bent on denying Arsenal from any and every angle imagineable. Sarina Wiegman will too, and she was in the stands to witness one of the finest displays of goalkeeping from a player she once called her No 1.

"She has a very uniquely competitive mindset," Izzy Christiansen reflected from the studio in north London. "She's in her element. Some of the saves were world class." Earps made eight of them. Five from inside the box.

But the best was left until last. In the final throws of the game, as the Gunners pushed to turn another unwanted home draw into something more, the ball found Frida Maanum on the edge of the area. She had already scored the game's opener but Arsenal had been undone 98 seconds later and needed another moment of inspiration.

With almost no backlift at all, Maanum shaped a lovely strike towards the top corner and waited to see it nestle in the net. Except it never did. Earps was forced to backpedal but got enough purchase on her leap to claw the ball onto the crossbar and preserve the point London City deserved for their efforts. None more impressive than her own.

Claims of vintage Earps echoed around the Emirates. Social media buzzed with posts of 'Mary's back!' The WSL is certainly a better league with her in it.

Wiegman may no longer be able to call upon the 33-year-old's services, but Eder Maestre will be delighted he can. If London City are to turn their Champions League ambitions into reality, Earps' wealth of big-game experience and ability to handle pressure moments could prove invaluable.

articles.title: From rugby powerhouse to bodybuilder: How a World Cup winner is confronting fears of CTE
articles.summary: Prompted by a long-term feeling he held that something wasn’t right, Phil Vickery underwent a brain scan two years ago, revealing damage to his brain. The former international sports star worried that it was chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE).
articles.body: Prompted by a long-term feeling he held that something wasn’t right, Phil Vickery underwent a brain scan two years ago, revealing damage to his brain. The former international sports star worried that it was chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE). The progressive, degenerative brain disease caused by repeated hits to the head is currently one of the biggest headlines across many high-impact, contact sports like boxing, hockey, American football and rugby – the sport where Vickery made his name. “100% – I know. I don’t have any doubts … I knew it before. There are no secrets for me. I knew that I was struggling,” the 2003 Rugby World Cup winner with England tells CNN Sports in the leafy county of Gloucestershire. CTE can only be definitively diagnosed only after death, but it has been associated with symptoms that overlap with dementia such as depression, anxiety, memory loss and lack of impulse control. Changes in the brain may begin before symptoms develop and not all people with the disease will have symptoms while alive. Vickery – who was a hulking, burly figure in his rugby days – admits that anger would initially take over when he struggled to remember simple things like names and places. He says his symptoms became more apparent to him “six or seven years ago.” “It’s not those that you, kind of – people you met a long time ago. You’re talking family members and people pretty close to you,” he explains. “You learn to get by and laugh about it [though]. I’ve moved into the space of, ‘What can I do to help myself?’” There seems something cruel, however, about its impact being felt at the place that for so long was his favorite stage – the home of England rugby – Twickenham. Sitting in the stands at England’s game against Australia recently, 50-year-old Vickery was forced to wear earplugs to drown out the noise and the overwhelming flood of emotion. The man who was involved in one of his country’s greatest ever sporting memories reveals he burst into tears in the parking lot as he went home. ‘My sister would look after me’ Even as CNN Sports speaks to him in the quiet, controlled environment of an indoor interview setup, Vickery says tinnitus in his ears is ringing like crazy. He lets out a humming noise to paint the picture of the sounds whirring around. And then there’s the question of Vickery’s own mortality. It’s a sobering moment when he acknowledges that there’s a chance his condition could deteriorate in the coming years, impacting those nearest and dearest to him. “It’s difficult because you tend to not really to talk about it,” he says as his voice begins to crack. “We do a little bit. My family are aware of it … I’ve got their support.” He then takes a long pause, looking down at his hands brushing against each other as his eyes fill with tears. “My sister would look after me which is amazing. My brother’s around. Mom’s still around,” he smiles, sits back and exhales. “I’m very fortunate that I have a platform, but there are lots of people who are suffering.” Landmark concussion lawsuit Vickery is one of more than 1,100 players – across both codes of rugby (league and union) – who claim that repeated impacts sustained throughout their careers have led to conditions such as CTE, Parkinson’s and motor neuron disease. They accuse World Rugby, the Rugby Football Union (RFU), the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU), the Rugby Football League (RFL) and others of failing in their duty of care to protect them from the risks of brain injury. The governing bodies have all vigorously denied liability. Though, the rugby legend holds no bitterness or malice regarding the situation he finds himself in. “I would do it (again) because I would never not do anything to play rugby,” he affirms. The legal process remains ongoing, but Vickery says there’s no winners or losers in it – nothing will change what he believes is his diagnosis. He maintains that it’s about accountability and integrity. “There are people who know a lot more than they let on. All I want is just some honesty,” he tells CNN Sports. “I would love to just get to court and for people’s stories to be heard. “Even if you win as a player, you get money, [but] it doesn’t change my diagnosis. It doesn’t take away from the problems. “What it does do is give comfort for people who will need looking after. “Silence isn’t a f**king defense. That I find very difficult to accept.” Bodybuilding transformation Vickery admits now that he found it very difficult to accept the end of his professional sporting career. “The nerves, the sense of pride, the emotion, ‘I’m going to be sick,’ ‘Am I good enough? Am I not good enough?’ The grumbles of the stadia, people, walking down that tunnel, fireworks, the noise…” Vickery recalls in vivid detail about that famed 2003 World Cup final. “Wow.” But inevitably that elation didn’t last forever. “I spent 10 or 12 years pretending with my rugby. I didn’t really deal with finishing the rugby, locked it away, put it in a dark cupboard, shut the door,” he reflects. “The mistake then for me is trying to find something to replace the irreplaceable.” So instead of that, he’s somewhat unexpectedly – and sensationally – found bodybuilding. Challenged by a former coach to perform at a show, Vickery details to CNN Sports how he underwent an 18-week preparation. Though he had to follow a strict diet and performance plan, the purity of his new sport made him fall in love with the process. “You’ll see it on Instagram someone who posts, ‘You can look like this in 12 weeks.’ No, you f**king can’t! No, you can’t. It takes a long time and a lot of effort,” he states. “There’s no smoke and mirrors. You can’t hide behind anything. You’re on stage wearing nothing. Your physique is a reflection of the commitment that you’ve put in.” Though competitors do actually wear something: a serious amount of fake tan and, in Vickery’s case, a shiny red Speedo. When the former England icon posted his pictures from a recent competition on social media, they almost broke the internet, such was the contrast from the images of his days playing rugby. And while he might have personally seen plenty of room for improvement, he hopes others find it inspiring. “It’s just a bit of inspiration. It’s not about making people bodybuilders,” Vickery jokes. “We’ve never been so connected as a society but yet we’ve never been so disconnected. “The messages I get from people talking about mental health or struggles means a lot. “So if you can make a difference to someone’s life, just one, it’s worth it.”

articles.title: El precioso gesto del Ceuta que en Tenerife nunca olvidarán
articles.standfirst: El equipo caballa no celebró su gol, que finalmente fue anulado: Jordi Escobar se arrodilló y mandó un beso al cielo, mientras recibía una tremenda ovación del Heliodoro.
articles.summary: El equipo caballa no celebró su gol, que finalmente fue anulado: Jordi Escobar se arrodilló y mandó un beso al cielo, mientras recibía una tremenda ovación del Heliodoro.
articles.body: El de ayer fue un día de emociones. De homenajes. Todo por Jesús de Miguel, en el regreso del Tenerife a la competición dos semanas después de tragedia. En el mismo escenario en que el futbolista cayó desplomado un día antes de perder la vida. La temporada va a ser muy dura para el equipo chicharrero. También lo está siendo para el Ceuta. No sólo por su delicada situación clasificatoria (colista, con 5 puntos de 42 posibles), sino por todo lo que ha ocurrido en los últimos meses y sigue ocurriendo en la ciudad autónoma. Quizás, por ello, nadie mejor que ellos para empatizar con la tragedia. En el minuto 30, el equipo caballa se adelantó en el marcador, cuando Kuki Zalazar dibujó una buena acción por la izquierda y Jordi Escobar la culminó con un magnífico primer toque. El tanto no valió porque la revisión del VAR lo acabó anulando por fuera de juego, pero la celebración quedará para siempre. El delantero, en la misma portería en la que Demi hizo goles vitales para el ascenso, se arrodilló, se santiguó y mandó un beso al cielo, rodeado por todos sus compañeros, mientras recibía una tremenda ovación del Heliodoro Rodríguez López en señal de agradecimiento. El Tenerife, que no vencía en Liga desde el 13 de septiembre, acabó ganando 2-0. Un triunfo para Jesús de Miguel. Eterno, por siempre.

articles.title: Güler construye su propio Imperio y hasta deja a Zidane con la boca abierta: "Es muy, muy, muy bueno"
articles.standfirst: Es el jugador de la Nations que más faltas recibe, el segundo que más dispara, el cuarto que más ocasiones genera...
articles.summary: Es el jugador de la Nations que más faltas recibe, el segundo que más dispara, el cuarto que más ocasiones genera...
articles.body: Arda Güler ya no es ninguna promesa. Es una realidad. El fantasista del Real Madrid, elegido 'Mejor Joven' de la pasada Champions League, continúa dando pasos de gigante tanto a nivel de club... como con su selección. Devolvió a Turquía a un Mundial 24 años después, pero ni el decepcionante papel de su país en la Copa del Mundo -acabó colista en un grupo con EE.UU., Australia y Paraguay- ni su pobre participación en la Nations League -ha terminado última de grupo con 0 puntos- han impedido que el ex de Fenerbahçe continúe brillando con luz propia. En sus últimos, con el Madrid y con Turquía, ha fabricado ocho partidos ha 'fabricado' nueve goles: ha marcado cinco y ha repartido cuatro asistencias. En la derrota ante Francia (2-1) volvió a dejar su sello: en el 53' vio cómo le anulaban un gol -era el 1-1- por fuera de previo de İsmail Yüksek y asistió desde el córner a Abdülkerim Bardakci en el 90' para que redujera distancias. "Arda Güler es fantástico. Juega en uno de los mejores clubes del mundo y es uno de los mejores futbolistas del mundo", aseguró Kevin de Bruyne tras su golazo de falta en la derrota ante Bélgica (1-2). Elogios a los que no dudó en sumarse Zinedine Zidane: "Turquía no me sorprendió. Cuando tienen el balón, son un equipo capaz de jugar bien. Son jugadores fantásticos con el balón. Arda es muy, muy, muy bueno". Su gol ante Bélgica y su asistencia frente a Francia no han servido para evitar el más que posible descenso de Turquía a la Liga B. Sin embargo, Güler, con los datos en la mano, bien podría optar a erigirse en el 'MVP' de esta Fase Liga. El '15' del Real Madrid es, según 'Opta', el jugador de Turquía que más disparos ha registrado (23), el que más 'key pases' -pases que acaban en tiro- ha brindado (11), el que más centros precisos ha realizado (7), el que más balones ha tocado en el área rival (26), el que más regates ha completado con éxito (13), el que más duelos ha ganado (47) y el que más faltas ha sufrido (27). No sólo brilla dentro de Turquía. Es el jugador que más faltas recibe de toda la Nations, el segundo que más dispara -sólo le supera Nikola Krstovic (26)- y el cuarto que más ocasiones de gol genera (5) y que más pases realiza con éxito en el último cuarto (114). Un paso al frente que algunos, en Turquía, piden que tenga un premio extra. "Necesitamos un líder en el vestuario. Los últimos seis partidos lo han demostrado: el capitán de este equipo no debería ser Hakan Çalhanoglu, debería ser Arda Güler, que lo da todo por la selección. El liderazgo y la responsabilidad no tienen edad, sólo quienes lo merecen", apunta Sabah. Su Imperio no deja de crecer.

articles.title: Jurgen Klopp says Fifa president Gianni Infantino worse than predecessor Sepp Blatter
articles.summary: Germany manager Jurgen Klopp says he "didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that" as he calls for Fifa president Gianni Infantino to be replaced.
articles.body:
Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp says he "didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that" as he called for Fifa president Gianni Infantino to be replaced.

Blatter resigned as Fifa boss in 2015 amid a corruption scandal and was succeeded by Infantino in February 2016.

Infantino plans to stand for re-election in March but has been under pressure since scrapping his Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which included selling off stakes in the World Cup and other Fifa competitions to private investors.

Infantino apologised to the Fifa Council for the plan but was told he was not fit to lead world football's governing body unless he released all the documents and answered key questions.

"I've been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense," said former Liverpool boss Klopp.

"I didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that."

Klopp added: "Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job."

French Football Federation (FFF) president Philippe Diallo has been named as Uefa's candidate to challenge Infantino.

Diallo received the unanimous support of Uefa's executive committee and formal ratification from the FFF is expected on Tuesday.

Uefa, which is European football's governing body, said it has "full confidence" Diallo would "uphold the highest standards of governance" amid its calls for "renewed unity and trust within the global football community".

Wenger decides not to challenge Fifa chief Infantino

Infantino apologises to Fifa Council - but told he is still not fit to lead

Uefa has been one of Infantino's fiercest critics and has repeatedly called on him to stand down.

It has prepared criminal legal proceedings against Infantino and lodged a claim in three US courts for all documents related to FFE to be released.

The deadline for candidates to officially confirm they are standing against Infantino in Fifa's presidential election is Wednesday.

Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who is Fifa's head of global development, had been considering running for the job but sources have told BBC Sport he has ruled himself out.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put his name forward in October.

Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also announced his intention to stand.

"There are people who truly care about the future of football - people who aren't driven by financial interests," said Klopp.

"If someone like that were to step up - if someone like that were to become president - I think that would be a significant improvement.

"There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it."

articles.title: Romelu Lukaku: Belgium striker announces retirement from international football
articles.summary: Romelu Lukaku retires from international football, saying he has "enjoyed every single moment" of playing for Belgium.
articles.body:
Romelu Lukaku has retired from international football, saying he has "enjoyed every single moment" of playing for Belgium.

Fenerbahce striker Lukaku, 33, made his international debut in 2010 and is Belgium's all-time leading men's goalscorer with 94 goals in 135 appearances.

He is the fifth highest men's international goalscorer of all time, behind Sunil Chhetri, Ali Daei, Lionel Messi and leader Cristiano Ronaldo, who has scored 146.

Lukaku scored eight goals across four World Cups, including in the run to the quarter-finals at this summer's tournament, and a total of six goals at three European Championships.

Writing on Instagram, , external the former Everton, Chelsea and Manchester United forward thanked his team-mates and coaches "for pushing and trusting me to help the team" during his 16 years with the national side.

He missed Belgium's Nations League win over Turkey last week with a hip injury and was an unused substitute on Sunday as they qualified for the last eight of the competition by beating Italy 4-1.

"These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team... I went through every emotion possible," Lukaku wrote.

"To the Belgium fans thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in four World Cups and three European Championships.

"I will never forget those moments. I'm at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing. It was enjoyable. I'm grateful."

In 2023, Lukaku scored 14 times in eight Euro 2024 qualifying appearances, breaking the record for goals scored by a player in a European Championship qualifying campaign.

His Belgium team-mate Kevin de Bruyne posted an image of himself with Lukaku , external on Instagram adding: "There are no words to describe what you've meant to me and our country!"

articles.title: Refuerzo de lujo para Flick
articles.standfirst: Dani Olmo se ha entrenado este lunes con el resto de sus compañeros
articles.summary: Dani Olmo se ha entrenado este lunes con el resto de sus compañeros
articles.body: No todo son malas noticias para Hansi Flick. Si el parón de selecciones ha devuelto tocados a Frenkie de Jong y Pau Cubarsí, el técnico alemán recupera a Dani Olmo para los próximos partidos. El delantero azulgrana se ha entrenado este lunes con el resto de sus compañeros y, salvo contratiempo, podrá jugar el próximo fin de semana frente al Villarreal. Olmo se lesionó en el partido de Champions League frente al PSG. Sufrió una pequeña rotura en el aductor izquierdo después de un choque con Vitinha durante el encuentro. Al día siguiente se le realizaron pruebas médicas que confirmaron la lesión y se estimó, aunque no de manera oficial, que el tiempo de baja sería de aproximadamente un mes. La recuperación ha evolucionado a muy buen ritmo y el delantero tenía muy buenas sensaciones desde hace unos días. De hecho, ha adelantado unos días su regreso a los entrenamientos respecto al plazo previsto. A falta de seis días para que se dispute el partido frente al Villarreal, todo apunta a que Olmo podrá participar en ese encuentro. Habrá que ver si Flick decide alinearlo en el once inicial o prefiere darle entrada durante el partido. Durante este mes en el que Olmo ha estado de baja, Fermín ha ocupado su lugar en todos los partidos, tanto con el Barcelona como con la selección.

articles.summary: The list of College Football Playoff contenders is dwindling as the 2026 regular season nears its conclusion.
articles.body:
The list of College Football Playoff contenders is dwindling as the 2026 regular season nears its conclusion.

With two weeks left before conference championship games, only Utah and UCLA are still undefeated. Just six others—including top-ranked Georgia—in a Power Four league hold a 9-1 mark, while Boise State and Liberty own the final one-loss records from a Group of Six conference.

At this point, the stakes in every game are awfully high.

After losing in Week 11, programs like Kentucky, Houston and LSU are feeling the sting of that disappointment, knowing their CFP chances are just about zero.

The projected bracket is a reflection of B/R's Top 25 dropped into the organization of the official CFP format.

Devon Dampier continued his terrific year, totaling 304 yards and four touchdowns in Utah's dramatic win at Arizona. Texas Tech, meanwhile, raced out to a 21-0 lead during the first quarter en route to a blowout of Oklahoma State on the road. Utah is a perfect 10-0 and all but officially headed to the Big 12 Championship, and Texas Tech is the only one-loss team in the conference.

The bells have tolled for LSU, which dropped to 6-4. Lane Kiffin's team squandered an eight-point lead in the fourth quarter as Texas won on Arch Manning's four-yard touchdown pass to Raleek Brown with two seconds remaining. The victory pushed Texas to 8-2 and one step closer to solidifying its CFP résumé.

The major upsets of the weekend now spell disaster for Houston, Kentucky and South Carolina. Since both UH and UK lack a truly signature win, three-loss records with no path to their respective league championships are a serious issue. South Carolina dropped its fourth game, a de facto eliminator.

1. Georgia 2. Utah 3. UCLA 4. Notre Dame 5. Miami 6. Indiana 7. Texas 8. Tennessee 9. Alabama 10. Wake Forest 11. Texas Tech 12. BYU 13. Boise State 14. Iowa 15. Oregon 16. Kentucky 17. Ohio State 18. USC 19. Arizona 20. Ole Miss 21. Liberty 22. Louisville 23. Houston 24. Memphis 25. UTSA

Seeding is a reflection of how B/R's Top 25 would shape the bracket.

Power 4 Champions and Top Group of 6 Team

Through two weeks of the College Football Playoff rankings, Boise State has been the only G6 team included.

Veteran quarterback Maddux Madsen threw for a career-high 371 yards and four touchdowns as Boise State held off Oregon State 46-41. Rasean Jones accounted for 230 of those yards, scoring three times on his 11 catches.

The victory punched Boise's ticket to the Pac-12 Championship Game, which will be played on the blue turf of the Broncos' home stadium.

Conference USA favorite Liberty is 9-1, while Memphis and UTSA are 8-2 in the American. Toledo (MAC) and Louisiana Tech (Sun Belt) are both 8-2, as well. The race to represent the G6 in the Playoff is not over.

But it's clear that Boise State is the unquestioned front-runner right now.

LSU's CFP hopes are effectively over, but the Tigers can play the spoiler role during a trip to Tennessee. On the other hand, the Vols could put themselves on the doorstep of the College Football Playoff with a victory. Tennessee is 8-2 and closes the regular season against Vanderbilt, which is 1-6 in the SEC and 4-6 overall.

Hey, uh, Iowa may sneak into the Playoff! After losses by Kentucky and Houston, the Hawkeyes should rise to about 13th in the next CFP rankings—just two spots from being on the correct side of the cut line. For that to happen, however, Iowa absolutely must defeat Illinois and Nebraska over the next two weeks.

On what's otherwise a pretty quiet Saturday, UCLA has an interesting game at Michigan. While the Bruins aren't a very convincing team offensively, they've been nothing short of outstanding on defense. Michigan will probably force a low-scoring game, so UCLA may need to win ugly again.

articles.title: Heisman Has a New Contender and 6 Other Overreactions After Week 11 of 2026 College Football Season
articles.summary: We're running out of weeks, and that's not an overreaction. It's a reality.
articles.body:
We're running out of weeks, and that's not an overreaction. It's a reality.

Schedules are winding down, conference championships will soon be played for the last time, and the College Football Playoff will crystalize soon enough.

As such, our weekly overreactions are becoming less reckless. The more football we see, the more we learn. And in Week 11, we learned plenty.

What stood out during a packed week of action? Let's dive in.

Wake Forest is Legit and Knocking on Playoff Door

We're well beyond the days of thinking Wake Forest is just a nice little team delivering a good story.

No, this team has earned something much more than that.

On Saturday, the Demon Deacons smothered SMU on the road 49-7, and the score doesn't do it justice. Wake Forest led 42-0 at half, and the second half essentially featured both teams running out the clock.

Quarterback Gio Lopez returned after suffering a knee injury, and he was solid despite clearly not playing at 100 percent. He didn't need to be fully healthy, as his team was dominant in every area.

As for the season, the Demon Deacons are 9-1 and the lone loss came against Miami. It was, and this matters to the College Football Playoff selection committee, a competitive game.

The team has games against Georgia Tech and Duke to close out the year, and the playoff is suddenly a very real possibility.

Dan Lanning Has Done One of His Finest Coaching Jobs Yet

Sounds weird, yes? We're talking about a team many, including this writer, picked to win a national title. That was not to be, and the season will still be a massive disappointment.

But it would be deeply unfair if we didn't give the Ducks—and more specifically Dan Lanning—credit for bringing this team back from the dead.

Oregon was sitting at 4-3, with star QB Dante Moore out for the season. Offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer was fired midyear. It would have been easy for the Ducks to pack things up right then and there and look ahead to 2027.

Wins over Northwestern, Ohio State and now Michigan, however, have given this team renewed purpose.

Yes, those wins deserve context. Michigan is a mess, and Ohio State is a shell of what we thought it would be at this point. Oregon hasn't gone out and conquered a slew of elite teams, although they've become a force of late.

Frankly, it says a lot about Lanning and his leadership. Things were quickly heading sideways, although Lanning did a masterful job keeping it together.

Devon Dampier Has Played His Way into the Heisman Race

Up until now, he's been making his case for the award week by week, largely out of sight. On Saturday night, or perhaps it was early Sunday morning for some, that changed.

Utah quarterback Devon Dampier lifted the Utes to a thrilling, back-and-forth victory over Arizona. The game featured more than 900 yards of offense, and he threw for more than 200 yards, ran for more than 100 yards and scored four touchdowns.

As such, Dampier should be considered a threat as he quarterbacks one of the last unbeaten teams.

It's been an odd season for the award, which felt like Jeremiah Smith's to lose early on. It might still be Smith's to lose, although the competition at quarterback is real. Notre Dame's CJ Carr and Miami's Darian Mensah have largely been considered the other contenders.

Utah plays TCU and West Virginia to close out the regular season before likely getting a crack at one last showcase in the Big 12 Championship Game.

He might not be the favorite, but Saturday night did plenty to help his late push.

Georgia Has Blossomed into a Massive Favorite to Win National Championship

Forget about what the odds say, although the odds like Georgia a lot as well.

The Bulldogs have morphed into a football machine since an inexplicable loss to Auburn, absolutely clobbering three ranked teams in a row.

Georgia jumped out to a 31-0 lead in the second quarter, and the Bulldogs essentially cruised from that point forward. They won 48-21, although they probably could have picked a score.

Georgia has now beaten four ranked teams this year, and it will close out the season with games at South Carolina and against Georgia Tech.

Offensively, quarterback Gunner Stockton is the perfect architect for a team that has weapons all over the place. And while the team has had better defenses, Kirby Smart has difference makers and speed at every level.

There's no secret formula. In fact, much of this is familiar through the era of NIL and the one that came before it. The constant through it all, of course, is Smart, who is in a strong position to add another championship to his trophy case.

Texas Just Locked Up a College Football Playoff Spot

It wasn't pretty or easy, but Texas found a way in the end.

The Longhorns delivered what essentially amounted to a walk-off 22-21 win against LSU, sealing the deal with a short Arch Manning touchdown pass with just seconds remaining.

Manning didn't play a pretty football game, either. He threw three ugly INTs and was regularly off the mark with his throws. When it mattered, though, he once again made a play.

Sure, the Longhorns have two regular season games left. They'll play Arkansas next week and then at Texas A&M to end the year. Both of these games should be wins, although nothing should be assumed this season.

A loss would be ugly, although it wouldn't doom this team.

The resume is absolutely superb. Texas has wins over five ranked teams already, and three of those wins have come on the road against teams ranked in the top 18.

It's not always easy on the eyes, and it doesn't have to be. It also doesn't matter.

Dabo Swinney's Future at Clemson Looks Increasingly Uncertain

It's been said before, and it'll be said again: The days of Clemson being a dominant football team under Dabo Swinney are gone.

No hot takes. No strong opinions. Just mountains of evidence that confirm this to be true.

The latest piece of evidence, however, is the most damning. Clemson lost to Georgia Tech at home 20-6, totaling just 228 yards of offense against a team that earned only its third win on Saturday.

The Tigers moved to 6-4 with the loss, and we might not be done there. Clemson plays at Duke and against South Carolina to end the season, and a 6-6 regular season could be in sight. This comes on the heels of a seven-win season in 2025.

At what point does Clemson ask the tough questions about its coach, even if it costs them a small fortune?

The Tigers would owe Swinney over $50 million if they fired him without cause today, which is an absurd amount of money. At what point, however, does the cost of falling short of the program's expectations outweigh a hefty buyout?

Clemson just reached a new rock bottom. It doesn't feel like the Tigers can go much deeper.

Coaches on the Hot Seat Had a Dreadful Week

It wasn't just Dabo Swinney getting heat after Week 11.

Luke Fickell and Shane Beamer both leave the week squarely on the hot seat after ugly losses.

Wisconsin lost to Maryland. South Carolina lost to Arkansas. Although both teams were favored by at least a touchdown, it didn't matter. And despite all the good both coaches have accomplished this year, these losses likely change the conversation.

For Fickell, this moment has been building. After starting the season 4-1, the Badgers are now 6-4. Granted, there's no shame in losing to UCLA and Iowa, especially on the road. But Wisconsin scored a combined seven points in those two games.

Losing to Maryland is a significant blow. Period. And if Wisconsin loses to either Purdue or Minnesota, well, things could get interesting.

As for South Carolina, a 34-6 defeat to Arkansas extended its losing streak to four games. Not having QB LaNorris Sellers didn't help, although that can't be an excuse given what we just saw.

The Gamecocks dropped to 6-4, and the news gets worse. South Carolina plays Georgia next week followed by Clemson. While it's a lot to ask, Beamer could desperately use an upset.

articles.title: Republic of Ireland v Kosovo: Irish captain Nathan Collins ruled out of must-win Nations League game
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland captain Nathan Collins is ruled out of Tuesday's must-win Nations League game against Kosovo with a knee injury.
articles.body:
Republic of Ireland captain Nathan Collins has been ruled out of Tuesday's must-win Nations League game against Kosovo with a knee injury.

Defender Collins picked up the issue in the closing stages of Saturday's 1-0 defeat by Austria in Linz and has returned to his club Brentford for treatment.

Queens Park Rangers' Jimmy Dunne will replace Collins - who also missed all four games of the September/October window - in the matchday squad for the Kosovo fixture.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has opted against drafting in Seamus Coleman, who is currently with the squad in a playing/coaching hybrid role.

"No, Jimmy Dunne will take Nathan's spot but we're really happy with what Seamus is giving to us," said Hallgrimsson.

"We obviously need to see the session today, that's the first session after the game, to see how players are but given everything I think we'll have the same squad including Jimmy."

Hallgrimsson rues 'painful' defeat for Republic of Ireland

The Republic of Ireland must win Tuesday's game to finish second in Group B3 and seal a place in March's promotion play-offs.

Hallgrimsson's side fell to a late 1-0 defeat by Kosovo in September before bouncing back to take four points from two matches against Israel.

"We need to get the same mentality, the same characters on the pitch against Kosovo," added Hallgrimsson.

"It is going to be as tough a game as it was in Austria, so just transfer that same attitude and if we do that, we will have a good byproduct, which is a win.

"It is clear we need to win the game, a draw will do nothing for us, and that is our mentality going into the game."

The Republic of Ireland's ultimate aim is securing a place at Euro 2028, which they will co-host alongside England, Wales and Scotland.

While goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher said playing in a tournament at home would be "amazing", he insisted the players are not looking that far ahead.

"Yeah, it would obviously be hard to describe, it would be an amazing experience, to play in a major tournament at home would be special," said the Brentford keeper.

"But I don't think we can think too far ahead into that. Obviously we've got to focus on tomorrow and trying to get a good result and we'll look towards that then when it comes.

"But we all know the opportunity that's there for us if we can perform, so it'll be a great opportunity."

articles.title: Women's FA Cup: Lye Town, Peterborough United and the never-ending tie
articles.summary: Nowadays, Women's FA Cup ties are decided on the day with extra time and penalties if needed. Unless that tie is Lye Town v Peterborough United.
articles.body:
In years gone by, it was not unusual for FA Cup ties to require three attempts to complete as every drawn match would require another replay.

Nowadays, Women's FA Cup ties are decided on the day with extra time and penalties if needed.

Unless that tie is Lye Town v Peterborough United in the first round of the 2026-27 competition.

The match between the Women's National League sides has now been abandoned twice, and is yet to be completed.

The first go was abandoned because of a serious player injury, while the second on Sunday was called off amid bad weather.

It means that while most teams remaining in the competition are awaiting the third-round draw on Monday evening - when second-tier WSL2 sides enter the competition - Lye and Peterborough are still stuck in round one.

Fourth-tier Lye, of National League Division One Midlands, already had an unusual path to round one to face Peterborough of the National League Northern Premier, a division above.

Entering in the third qualifying round, their match against Coton Green was also postponed, so took place on October 22, after the first-round draw had been made.

A 5-0 win set up the Peterborough tie, due to be played on 8 November, a week after the other games.

It finally looked like the tie would be played to a conclusion as Lye led 1-0 with 12 minutes remaining.

But after a serious injury suffered by Lye goalkeeper Pharyn Ashton the match was abandoned and rescheduled again for 15 November.

This too proved in vain. Sunday's match was abandoned at half-time with Peterborough leading 3-1, because of a waterlogged pitch.

Spare a thought too for Rugby Borough, who are lined up to play the winner in round two but are also being forced to wait.

articles.title: Ian Evatt: Blackpool boss laments diarrhoea-hit side's loss to AFC Wimbledon
articles.summary: Blackpool boss Ian Evatt says his squad had a horrific build-up to Saturday's League One defeat by AFC Wimbledon following a fast-spreading sickness bug in his camp.
articles.body:
Blackpool boss Ian Evatt has revealed his squad had a horrific build-up to their defeat by fellow League One strugglers AFC Wimbledon following a fast-spreading sickness bug in his camp.

The Seasiders were without 15 players and staff for Saturday's visit to the capital as they suffered from "severe diarrhoea and vomiting", with some suffering such symptoms when playing.

Evatt's side lost 1-0 at the Cherry Red Records Stadium - their seventh league defeat of the season - and are now 20th and only outside the bottom four on goal difference.

"There's some players and staff that haven't been able to to make it out of bed," Evatt told BBC Radio Lancashire.

"Some staff have had to continue to do their jobs with the vomiting and the diarrhoea and the players are the same - some players were vomiting on the pitch [or had] diarrhoea on the pitch. It's been horrific.

"I've got to be honest, I've never seen a virus spread so fast, I've never seen anything as aggressive as what it is."

Smith strike earns Wimbledon win over Blackpool

Evatt said the effects of the virus began by midday on Friday, the day before the fixture, and suspected its effects had its origins at their Squires Gate training facility.

Blackpool have now won just one game out of their past 10 League One fixtures with their opponents ending a poor run of form themselves, having not won in seven attempts prior to Saturday's fixture.

"We did everything we could, we followed every protocol we could, we followed every process, we separated players, we separated staff but it was continuing to spread," Evatt added.

"There's even staff that have had the virus that haven't even travelled with us so it's obviously something that's been picked up and started at Squires and it just snowballed fast.

"We did what we could in terms of following protocol and processes with what we were asked to do but obviously the game still went ahead and in my opinion it shouldn't have."
