articles.title: Scotland: Andy Robertson to cap it all and take King Kenny Dalglish's crown
articles.summary: Andy Robertson will take over from Kenny Dalglish as Scotland's most-capped player when he captains his country against Switzerland on Monday evening.
articles.body:
Andy Robertson will become the most capped men's Scotland international if he earns his 103rd cap in Monday night's Nations League campaign closer in Switzerland.

Twelve years on from his debut - off the bench in a Poland friendly - he is set to surpass his friend and fellow Liverpool legend, Kenny Dalglish, whose record haul has stood for 40 years.

On moving level with the man they - and he - will always call King, the Tottenham Hotspur left-back shifted chat towards the former forward, his commendable humility laid bare.

But, in St Gallen, the spotlight will be brightly shone on one of Scotland's favourite sons as he goes solo at the summit.

Robertson set to make history, but hero Dalglish will always be King

Inside the fairytale journey of Scotland captain Robertson

For much of this year, Dalglish was the only man to have pulled on the navy blue of Scotland more times than Robertson.

'King Kenny' topped the list on 102 caps - earning his last in November 1986 against Luxembourg when in a player-manager role at Liverpool.

Few since have even come close to toppling him - even when Robertson does, he is keen to stress the throne is still reserved for Dalglish - but it is perhaps fitting it is the current captain, given their great friendship.

Which allows Dalglish to say he's not having any of it.

"He always says: 'You've got millions more games. Nations League, what's that? They didn't have that in my day!'" Robertson joked on the Stick to Football podcast recently.

"I think he might bring up a ratio for years-to-games-played so he's still on top.

"It's obviously something that's been on my radar for a while now. When you get to 80-odd caps, you start to look up."

Dalglish can console himself that his record of 30 goals - held jointly with Denis Law - is safely out of Robertson's reach.

But not out of John McGinn's - the midfielder's double against North Macedonia on Friday having taken him to within six of the legendary duo.

The Aston Villa captain is lurking only eight caps behind Robertson on the all-time caps list, too, so the Scotland men's centurion club could have three members soon.

Scotland's greatest captain? With a good Fifa card...

Since being given the armband by Alex McLeish after Scott Brown retired in 2018, Robertson has captained Scotland 32 times more than any other player.

At the time, he had earned just 22 caps and was just 24 but had established himself as Liverpool's left-back as they reached the Champions League final.

Now he is the only man to have led Scotland out at three major finals, reaching the milestone at the World Cup this summer.

Scotland and Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay enthused: "He's such a great captain and he's got that good balance between being one of the senior players and saying you need to wake up if you're not playing well.

"Then he's also got the personable side, organising things with the manager, helping young players and stuff. He's brilliant with that, brilliant."

One of those young players is 20-year-old Findlay Curtis, who told the media the night before Robertson's potentially-historic night that his captain has "probably been the biggest role model" he's looked up to since joining the international set-up earlier this year.

Perhaps that was because Robertson did him a turn back in the day. Unbeknownst to the skipper.

Rangers winger Curtis was only 14 during the Covid pandemic and was partial to playing a bit of Fifa, and Robertson was a star in his team.

"I was just thinking, I had him in my Fifa team," he explained. "[For] defending and he was just fast as well.

"What a servant he has been for the country."

Robertson has played under four permanent Scotland team bosses in his 12-year international career.

It was Strachan who plucked him from the under-21s to hand him his debut as a 19-year-old in a win over Poland in March 2014.

McLeish made him captain in 2018, calling Robertson the "outstanding candidate" and an "inspirational figure" - and now he has played five times for new boss Sebastien Pocognoli.

He even played one game under interim manager Malky Mackay in a friendly against the Netherlands at Pittodrie in 2017 as the Scottish FA searched for Strachan's replacement.

However, it is Steve Clarke's seven-year stint that Robertson will be mainly associated with, as the pair led Scotland to three major tournaments.

Robertson played 68 times for Clarke, all of them as captain, and the recently departed head coach consistently praised his figurehead.

"He's been a fantastic captain for Scotland," Clarke said at the World Cup.

"He's worked ever so hard for the country and he leads the group like the leader he is - and he's very, very important to me and the squad."

Over the piece, Robertson's caps are spread fairly evenly among friendlies and qualification games.

Crucially, though, he has also played nine times in major tournaments. What will rankle with him is there is only one win among those nine - June's victory over Haiti in Boston at the World Cup.

Overall, though, Robertson's Scotland career can be characterised by consistency.

He has started 100 of his 102 caps, rarely ever being substituted. He has not missed a camp in three years.

The only question seems to be how many Scotland caps will Robertson end up with?

At 32 and still playing in the Premier League, it appears there will be plenty more to come.

articles.title: European Soccer Clubs Group Files Complaint in Brussels Against UEFA and Storied Rivals
articles.summary: BRUSSELS (AP) — Another soccer politics dispute was sent to the European Union on Monday as lower-ranked clubs challenged storied rivals' close ties to UEFA.
articles.body:
BRUSSELS (AP) — Another soccer politics dispute was sent to the European Union on Monday as lower-ranked clubs challenged storied rivals' close ties to UEFA.

The 140-member Union of European Clubs (UEC) said it filed a complaint to the European Commission in Brussels about UEFA's legal working agreement through 2033 with the influential European Football Clubs group led by Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser al-Khelaifi. The EFC currently represents about 800 European clubs.

The Brussels-based UEC argues that EFC's exclusive access to UEFA to negotiate competition entries and how to allocate billions of euros (dollars) in prize money is bad for competitive balance and helps a small circle of clubs stay on top in the Champions League.

The UEC's arguments — about anti-competitive business practices and abuse of a dominant position — echo those by European Super League clubs when they won a 2023 ruling against UEFA and FIFA at the European Court of Justice in Luxembourg.

"This case is about using European competition law to protect the European sports model of genuinely open and balanced competitions," said the UEC's adviser on the complaint, Miguel Maduro, an independent governance expert once ousted by FIFA.

The clubs' complaint is the second soccer filing now with the European Commission.

In 2024, the European Leagues group joined with the Europe division of global players' union FIFPRO alleging FIFA fails to consult properly on decisions that are to its commercial benefit, including expanding its competitions. FIFPRO later reached agreement with FIFA to withdraw.

Since launching in 2023, the UEC's members include Union Saint-Gilloise, Levante, Osasuna, Burnley, St. Pauli and Aberdeen.

One of its key proposals not adopted by UEFA has been to share 5% of annual revenues from the three European club competitions among teams who trained the players taking part.

The clubs' group suggested that policy would have shared 67 million euros ($74 million) last season among clubs outside of top-tier divisions.

articles.title: La reconquista de Bellingham: "Perdí la sonrisa, me sentí un poco como el chivo expiatorio"
articles.standfirst: Los seis goles y 10 asistencias que suma con el Madrid e Inglaterra vuelve a situarle entre los mejores del mundo
articles.summary: Los seis goles y 10 asistencias que suma con el Madrid e Inglaterra vuelve a situarle entre los mejores del mundo
articles.body: Jude Bellingham ha recuperado la alegría. "Venía de un año algo difícil, pero aprendí mucho sobre mí mismo. Aprendí cosas que puedo hacer para hacerme la vida más fácil. Siempre me esfuerzo al máximo para ser cada vez mejor", reconocía a principios de octubre, después de golear a la República Checa (3-0). La lesión en el hombro no le ayudó. "Decidí seguir sin operarme y fue un error", admitía. Las críticas, tampoco. "Perdí la sonrisa jugando como Inglaterra después de la Eurocopa. Me sentí un poco como el chivo expiatorio. Creo que me trataban un poco mal en comparación con lo que aportaba", afirmaba. "Me ponía muy tenso y estresado y empecé a hablar con alguien que me ayudó a manejar ese tipo de cosas", confiesa a 'British Vogue'. En enero, tras la salida de Xabi Alonso, contestó a los que cuestionaban su vida nocturna 'empinando el codo' para festejar su gol al Mónaco (6-1): "Mucha gente dice muchas cosas. Puedes llorar o disfrutarlo. Les devolví la broma a los fans. Sé la verdad". El Mundial le sirvió de punto de inflexión. Sumó siete goles -sólo Mbappé (10) y Messi (8) marcaron más- y una asistencia auparon a Inglaterra al tercer puesto. Fue el jugador más destacado, por encima de Harry Kane. De hecho, en la antesala del Balón de Oro, fue elegido ''Mejor jugador de la selección masculina de Inglaterra' por segunda temporada consecutiva. "Creo que fue uno de los jugadores del torneo, no sólo para nosotros, sino de todo el Mundial. Estuvo a la altura de todo su potencial; simplemente podías ver qué competidor es y qué máquina es. Se crece bajo presión, le encantan estos momentos, le encantan estos escenarios y eso hace que dé lo mejor de sí", apuntaba Thomas Tuchel. Un buen momento al que Bellingham está dando continuidad. En este inicio de curso ha 'fabricado' ya 16 goles. Suma cinco goles y cuatro asistencias en 16 encuentros con el Real Madrid y acumula un tanto y seis pases de gol -lidera el ránking de asistentes de la Nations League- en seis compromisos con Inglaterra. En el triunfo ante España (2-3) en el Metropolitano volvió a echarse el equipo a la espalda. De una de sus cabalgadas 'marca de la casa' nació el córner que derivó en el 0-2 de Ezri Konsa y sirvió en bandeja el tercero a Ben White. De hecho, se convirtió en el primer jugador de Inglaterra en registrar siete asistencias en un año natural desde 1980. Rescatar únicamente eso sería quedarse en la superficie. Bellingham estuvo omnipresente. Apareció por todas partes en los 83 minutos que disputó. Fue el jugador de Inglaterra que más regates completó con éxito (5) y el que más duelos a ras de suelo ganó (10/11). Registró, además, dos disparos a puerta, tres recuperaciones y generó dos ocasiones de gol. "¡Qué noche!", posteó un Bellingham que, por momento de forma, vuelve a situarse como uno de los mejores futbolistas del mundo. La llegada de José Mourinho también le ha ayudado. “Antes jugaba más adelantado, en ese rombo del mediocampo, con dos extremos. En mi segunda temporada jugué más por la izquierda, entrando hacia adentro. Y con Arbeloa y Xabi, un poco más retrasado. Puedo jugar en varias posiciones y en cierto modo, soy víctima de esa versatilidad”, admitía el pasado curso. Mou le ha vuelto a acercar al área: "Un jugador de esa calidad tiene que estar cerca de la portería. Para mí, eso es obvio. Es único y sumamente importante para el equipo. Posee diversas cualidades: físicas, mentales, tácticas, capacidad para recuperar el balón, marcar goles, su habilidad en el juego aéreo... Es increíble”. Una decisión que está dando dividendos. "Por encima de todo, estoy disfrutando del fútbol. Estoy intentando dar lo mejor de mí para seguir mejorando cada día. Cuando te sientes bien y tienes confianza, quieres intentar cosas", insiste Bellingham. La reconquista continúa.

articles.standfirst: El futbolista argentino del FC Ezeiza fue operado de urgencia y también jugaba en la reserva de fútbol sala de Nueva Estrella, que suspendió toda su jornada deportiva
articles.summary: El futbolista argentino fue operado de urgencia y también jugaba en la reserva de fútbol sala de Nueva Estrella, que suspendió toda su jornada deportiva
articles.body: Abel Núñez, futbolista juvenil del FC Ezeiza, falleció este domingo tras sufrir un golpe en la cabeza durante un partido. El balón le impactó de lleno después de un rechace y el jugador cayó al césped sin reaccionar. Recibió allí las primeras atenciones y fue trasladado poco después a un centro médico. El encuentro se suspendió de inmediato, al igual que el de sexta división que debía disputarse a continuación. El FC Ezeiza, que milita en el Promocional Amateur, informó en un primer comunicado de que Núñez había pasado por el quirófano. “Está atravesando un momento muy difícil, luego de sufrir un fuerte golpe en la cabeza que requirió una intervención quirúrgica”, explicó el club, que pidió a familiares, amigos y aficionados que se sumaran a una cadena de oración. El estado del jugador no mejoró tras la operación y el club confirmó su muerte en redes sociales. “La noticia más dura que nos toca comunicar como club. Con un profundo dolor y una tristeza inmensa, despedimos a un chico que tenía toda una vida por delante y que hoy nos deja un vacío imposible de explicar”, escribió la entidad. El FC Ezeiza trasladó su pésame a la familia, los amigos y los compañeros del futbolista. “Que descanses en paz. Siempre serás parte de nuestra familia”, cerró el comunicado. Núñez también jugaba al fútbol sala en la reserva de Nueva Estrella, en la competición de la AFA. El club suspendió toda su jornada deportiva, incluido el encuentro ante Argentinos Juniors, y expresó su apoyo a la familia del jugador y a sus compañeros. “Hoy no hay partidos ni resultados que importen. Hoy el dolor nos une y nos invita a estar cerca de quienes más lo necesitan. Abel siempre será parte de nuestra familia. Descansa en paz, pequeño. Nueva Estrella nunca te va a olvidar”, publicó el club.

articles.title: Mary McAteer: Ipswich boss praises Wales international's football brain
articles.summary: Ipswich Town boss David Wright praised the football intelligence of Wales international Mary McAteer following her first goal for the club.
articles.body:
Ipswich Town boss David Wright praised the football intelligence of Wales international Mary McAteer following her first goal for the club.

McAteer joined Town on loan from Charlton Athletic in September as part of a revamp of the squad following last season's ninth-place finish in Women's Super League 2.

She headed home the rebound after skipper Maria Boswell's fierce shot came back off the crossbar against Watford and they went on to win Sunday's game 2-1.

The victory put Town third - and in the play-off places - in only their second season at that level.

"Every time Bos gets the ball in that area now, in my head I'm thinking, 'just shoot'," Wright told BBC Radio Suffolk.

"Mary is a really intelligent footballer - she uses her intelligence to find space between the lines, it allows her link through the thirds, and it's another sign of her intelligence that when Bos hits a beautiful strike, it hits the bar, bounces down, she's the first one to react and nods it in."

Ipswich on 'inevitable' path to WSL - Boswell

Kit Graham added Ipswich's second as they bounced back positively from a 2-1 home league defeat by Bristol City and midweek loss to McAteer's parent club Charlton in the Players' Cup.

"It has been a really tough week, not just physically, but also psychologically - three different challenges," said Wright.

"What good teams do is they bounce back. To finish the week off, going to Watford and coming away with three points, the girls should be really proud of themselves."

Boswell said last month that she believes it is "inevitable" that Town will eventually achieve their goal of a place in the top flight of English women's football.

But despite their current position, Wright insisted it was not a focus for him.

"I don't really look at the table. I want to push them, make them better and if we do that we will keep moving in the right direction - that process is getting better every day and will help us achieve what we want to achieve," he said.

Wright's side have won five of their eight WSL 2 games but now have over a month to wait before the next, when they travel to bottom-of-the-table Durham.

"I was looking at the calendar on the wall and I've never known such a big gap. The good thing is we've got lots of games in between so we'll be busy and when the Durham game comes round, the girls will be ready," Wright added.

articles.title: Has James Trafford replaced Jordan Pickford as England No 1?
articles.summary: James Trafford was given a chance to stake his claim as England's new number one - and away to the world champions, he absolutely took it.
articles.body:
As he was mobbed by his England team-mates for a late double save that secured a memorable 3-2 win against world champions Spain, the debate that followed about who the country's number one is was inevitable.

The Leeds keeper was given his chance to show England boss Thomas Tuchel what he could do again - and he absolutely took it.

On his fifth England cap the 24-year-old enjoyed a magnificent performance in Madrid as his side handed the hosts their first loss in 43 matches.

Trafford made four key saves in the final 12 minutes of the game, including an incredible double stop to first deny a Lamine Yamal curler and then dive again to his right to keep out Fermin Lopez from close range.

But after full-time in Spain Tuchel told ITV Sport "there's no number one" and Trafford had "a brilliant match".

So, following his performance on Sunday night, is Trafford now likely to oust Pickford as England's go-to goalkeeper?

Despite being just 24 years old Trafford has already been England's most expensive goalkeeper by transfer fee... twice.

Trafford returned to his boyhood Manchester City from Burnley for a £31m fee in 2025 and then left the Etihad for Leeds for £45m this summer - having been limited to being Pep Guardiola's 'cup goalkeeper'.

Given the downturn in form of their current goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, many City fans may well be wishing Trafford had stayed. Their loss is Leeds' - and maybe England's - gain.

At Leeds he has found his form and this season ranks first among the 52 goalkeepers who have played at least 10 games in Europe's big five leagues by save percentage (81.4%).

He has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026, and has rotated with Pickford across the Three Lions' five matches since the World Cup.

Pickford has started against Czech Republic and Croatia twice whereas Trafford has played against Czech Republic and started both England's matches with Spain, home and away.

After England's win in Madrid, which was the first time Spain had lost in the city in 39 years, Trafford's double-save was praised by his Three Lions team-mate Declan Rice.

"Everything happened so quick so for him to make two in the space of two seconds is massive," he told ITV. "A massive night for him."

Spain manager Luis de la Fuente agreed. He said: "We did generate some chances but England's goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last 10 or 15 minutes."

After the double-save several England players ran over to celebrate with Trafford.

And on Tuchel's decision to rotate between his two keepers former Manchester United captain Roy Keane told ITV: "I think it's smart management.

"This is the perfect time for Trafford to come in, against top players, and show what he's capable of doing."

Social media has been full of the 'England number one' debate since, with many suggesting this was a moment that marked the changing of the guard.

Could Tuchel really now not start with Trafford for England's Nations League quarter-finals? Only time will tell.

What about Pickford though? England's undisputed first choice for almost 10 years has rarely let his country down.

The 32-year-old has won 94 caps for England since making his debut in a 0-0 draw with Germany in 2017 and during his time as number one England have reached two World Cup semi-finals and two Euros finals.

According to Opta stats, Pickford has only made two errors leading to goals across his England career, with 46 clean sheets and a 74.3% save ratio.

And since the start of the 2024-25 season, only Arsenal's title-winning keeper David Raya has more clean sheets in the league than Pickford at Everton.

"We saw the last selections and all thought Jordan Pickford's place is under threat and James Trafford is going to be the next number one. I don't think Thomas Tuchel saw it as starkly or simply as that," said former England number one goalkeeper Paul Robinson to BBC Sport before England's win against Spain

"It's a conversation that will definitely take place down the road, but not now. Jordan is England's first choice, in my opinion, rightfully so given his consistency and performances over such a long period.

"This is a debate and conversation for the future definitely because Father Time catches up with everyone eventually and the manager needs to have a contingency plan, but Jordan Pickford very much remains number one and Thomas Tuchel has said as much.

"I don't think Jordan Pickford is under threat for his jersey on a permanent basis any time soon, irrespective of the next selection."

This isn't a debate that is going away any time soon. But having two goalkeepers genuinely competing for that number one shirt can only be to England's benefit.

articles.title: Luis Rubiales está de 'vuelta'
articles.standfirst: El castigo del TAD vence este martes, casi tres meses después del de la FIFA. El expresidente de la RFEF sigue investigado en el caso Supercopa
articles.summary: El castigo del TAD vence este martes, casi tres meses después del de la FIFA. El expresidente de la RFEF sigue investigado en el caso Supercopa
articles.body: Luis Rubiales cumple este martes 17 de noviembre los tres años de inhabilitación que le impuso el Tribunal Administrativo del Deporte (TAD) por su conducta en la final del Mundial femenino de 2023. Con la sanción de la FIFA también cumplida, el expresidente de la RFEF podrá volver a optar a un cargo federativo de ámbito estatal si reúne los requisitos del puesto. Por ahora, Rubiales no ha anunciado ningún proyecto para regresar al fútbol. El TAD le impuso dos sanciones de 18 meses. La primera, por el beso no consentido a Jenni Hermoso durante la entrega de medallas en Sídney, tras el primer título mundial de España. La segunda, por llevarse las manos a los genitales en el palco para celebrar la victoria. La FIFA le suspendió de forma provisional el 26 de agosto de 2023 y después le prohibió ejercer cualquier actividad relacionada con el fútbol, dentro y fuera de España. El Tribunal Arbitral del Deporte (TAS) confirmó el castigo en febrero de 2025. La sanción venció el pasado 26 de agosto. La Audiencia Nacional confirmó en junio de 2025 la condena por agresión sexual. La sentencia impuso a Rubiales una multa de 10.800 euros y el pago de 3.000 euros a Hermoso por daños morales. También ratificó su absolución del delito de coacciones. El expresidente recurrió la condena ante el Tribunal Supremo para pedir su absolución. Según informó Europa Press en septiembre, el alto tribunal preveía resolver el recurso antes de que acabara 2026. Rubiales sigue investigado en el caso Supercopa. El juzgado de Majadahonda examina el contrato que llevó el torneo a Arabia Saudí y otras operaciones de la Federación durante su mandato, entre ellas la adjudicación de las obras de reforma del estadio de La Cartuja. En junio, la jueza prorrogó la instrucción otros seis meses. Desde su salida de la RFEF, Rubiales ha publicado Matar a Rubiales y ha opinado en distintas entrevistas sobre la gestión de la Federación y el Mundial de 2030. En noviembre de 2025 aseguró que había hablado con dos federaciones asiáticas sobre posibles funciones de gestión, sin dar sus nombres. El pasado septiembre, en El Primer Palo, dijo que no pensaba volver a la presidencia y situó entre sus prioridades a su familia, sus negocios y su defensa judicial.

articles.title: Jesús Velasco, 2029
articles.standfirst: En el acto de la presentación de la renovación, Rafael Louzán, presidente de la Federación Española valoró la renovación: "Es el día de Jesús. Ahí hay dos títulos, pero lo bueno está por llegar".
articles.summary: En el acto de la presentación de la renovación, Rafael Louzán, presidente de la Federación Española valoró la renovación: "Es el día de Jesús. Ahí hay dos títulos, pero lo bueno está por llegar".
articles.body: Suspendida en su momento por el terrible accidente ferroviario de Urda, hoy se ha celebrado en la Ciudad del Fútbol de Las Rozas, la renovación del seleccionador nacional de fútbol sala, Jesús Velasco, hasta 2029. En el cargo desde el 1 de noviembre de 2024, Velasco ha completado dos años triunfales de España, especialmente este 2026, en el que la selección nacional conquistó la Eurocopa de Letonia, Lituania y Eslovenia, en Ljubljana ante Portugal (3-5) y la 'Finalissima', hace apenas ocho días, en el Arena de Niterói, en el que sus jugadores, tras firmar un 'Maracanazo' se alzaron con el título en y ante Brasil (0-3). Ahora el próximo objetivo, no puede ser otro que la tercera estrella, para la que España viaja a Kumanovo, donde se medirá a Macedonia del Norte, el próximo 8 de diciembre (19:00) en el segundo partido de la 'Main Round' hacia el Mundial de 2028. Saúl Ramos, conductor del acto, recordó los logros de Velasco en estos dos años antes de dar paso a un vídeo en el que se recordó esta etapa, ya en la historia del fútbol sala español y de su selección. Para valorar la renovación, Saúl dio paso a don Rafael Louzán, presidente de la Federación Española de Fútbol, y José Miguel Monje, presidente del Comité Nacional de Fútbol Sala. "Es el día de Jesús y, mirando a los dos trofeos que tenemos ahí, en un tiempo relativamente corto ha logrado devolver la ilusión al fútbol sala español. Llevabámos un tiempo ahí, no sé, hibernando, sin títulos y con la llegada de Jesús nos ha devuelto la ilusión, nos ha devuelto los títulos. Es un momento para estar orgulloso del acierto de la casa de nombrar a Jesús como el encargado de llevar a la selección. Desde que le conocí, noté su firmeza. Hay dos títulos, pero lo bueno está por venir", afirmó Louzán en su comparecencia. "Hagamos el equipazo que queremos hacer para que los éxitos lleguen, y de su mano, estoy convencido de que llegarán. Va a disponer de un espacio para trabajar cómodamente, se va a invertir 5 millones de euros para renovar el pabellón, lo que le va a permitir trabajar. El esfuerzo de la RFEF empieza por mejorar la instalación básica, tanto para el fútbol sala masculino como el femenino. Unas obras que deben finalizar en unos meses y hablaremos con ellos para se adapten a su trabajo", añadió Louzán. Mientras, José Miguel Monje, presidente del Comité Nacional, valoró la trayectoria de Jesús Velasco. "La Real Federación tiene la obligación de tener a los mejores. Es una bocanada de aire fresco. No sólo por los títulos, sino la forma cómo se está ganando: una forma agradable, bonita. Se queda sin cinco jugadores y los cinco jóvenes que ha incorporado han dado un nivel tremendo. Ha conseguido que los nuestros sean un equipo y una familia. Y los resultados están llegando. Vamos a ir a por todas. España tiene que estar en fútbol y fútbol sala entre los cuatro mejores. Luego, los títulos son cuestión de detalles". Carlos Ortiz, Sergio Lozano, Mario Rivillos, Adolfo, leyendas y jugadores en activo en el caso de los dos últimos felicitaron al seleccionador y recordaron algunas anécdotas de las que han vivido en los años que han trabajado a sus órdenes, recalcando el "placer de estar contigo", concluyó Adolfo. Fue el momento de Jesús Velasco: "Me váis a tener que echar de aquí. Era mi sueño que ahora estoy cumpliendo". De la tecnología dijo: "La dejo en manos de gente que está más capacitada que yo". Se juega como se entrena, en palabras de Jesús Velasco: "Tenemos una identidad muy clara, el juego de alta intensidad. Para conseguirlo, tienes que entrenar con alta intensidad, pero lo que no puedes provocar es que un jugador lesione a otro en un entrenamiento, ya en un partido es terrible, más en un entrenamiento". Los nueve meses de éxito: "No se nos van a olvidar. Esto lo tenemos aquí y lo vamos a recordar siempre. Como ganar con la selección, no hay nada". Otra leyenda, Ricardinho, que trabajó a sus órdenes. "Le deseo lo mejor y ojalá que no ganes mucho contra Portugal, pero si no gana Portugal, que ganes, que te lo mereces". Del Mundial, dijo Velasco: "Todavía no estamos allí, nos lo tenemos que ganar. Nos lo pondrán muy difícil, pero somos España y tenemos que demostrar que podemos ganar".

articles.title: Nike Replaces Adidas for New Champions League Ball After 25 Years, Watch Hype Teaser Video
articles.summary: Nike announced Monday it will be the official match ball supplier for UEFA's club competitions, including the Champions League, beginning next season.
articles.body:
Nike announced Monday it will be the official match ball supplier for UEFA's club competitions, including the Champions League, beginning next season.

Adidas has produced the match balls UEFA-sanctioned tournaments going to back to 2001. Nike was the designer in the four years before that and now returns to the role.

"We are excited and honoured to return to the UEFA Champions League, one of football's biggest stages, after more than two decades, and to bring Nike match balls across UEFA's men's club competitions, including all three major competitions for the first time," said Camilo Andrade, Nike Football's vice president and general manager, per ESPN.com .

The Athletic's Adam Crafton reported the sponsorship deal will be worth around $45 million annually.

articles.title: Ibai Gómez convierte al Zaragoza en un 4x4
articles.standfirst: Los maños son un todoterreno que gana en cualquier campo y ya ha anotado cuatro goles en cuatro partidos distintos en Liga
articles.summary: Los maños son un todoterreno que gana en cualquier campo y ya ha anotado cuatro goles en cuatro partidos distintos en Liga
articles.body: Cuando el Real Zaragoza descendió hace unos meses, había mucho temor por la categoría y los campos donde tendría que jugar. No solo se ha adaptado en tiempo récord sino que ha demostrado desenvolverse a la perfección en cualquier territorio. Estadios grandes, pequeños o medianos. No importa. Ibai Gómez ha logrado un equipo capaz de vencer a cualquier sean las circunstancias que sean. Por eso, este Real Zaragoza es un todoterreno que lidera su grupo de forma sólida y empieza a meter miedo a sus rivales. Once partidos sin caer, 25 goles a favor y cuatro puntos de ventaja sobre el segundo. Sus delanteros no están brillando pero está demostrando tener una pegada tremenda. Sin ir más lejos, los cuatro tantos que anotó en Jaén no sorprende. Es la cuarta vez que marca esas dianas en Liga en este curso. Primero lo hizo en Torremolinos en la victoria por 3-4, después le endosó cuatro al Teruel en el Ibercaja Estadio y repitió el mismo número frente al Atlético Madrileño. Además, en Copa también lo hizo con otros cuatro tanto contra el Tudelano. Ibai tiene a todo su equipo enchufado y no quiere parar. Su máquina está cada vez más engrasada y asesta golpes certeros a sus rivales en momentos claves como ocurrió en Jaén. Este todoterreno quiere seguir superando obstáculos en su camino hacia Segunda.

articles.title: Infantino made things worse at FIFA than Blatter, says Jurgen Klopp
articles.summary: The Germany coach believes anyone who replaces the FIFA president should care deeply about the future of football.
articles.body:
Germany coach Jurgen Klopp has called for an end to Gianni Infantino’s time as FIFA president, saying he “did not think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter”.

Klopp believes the next candidate for the job of leading football’s global governing body should have the game’s interests at heart.

“I’ve been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense,” Klopp said on Sunday in Berlin ahead of his team’s Nations League clash with the Netherlands .

“I didn’t think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that.”

President of FIFA from 1998, Blatter resigned in disgrace in 2015 amid corruption allegations. He later faced charges before being cleared in two trials, but was banned from football by FIFA’s ethics committee.

Klopp added: “Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.”

Swiss-born Infantino, who succeeded Blatter as FIFA president in 2016, has been criticised for a series of decisions and proposals, including his plan to sell off part of the commercial rights of the World Cup. He was also lambasted for last year’s creation of the FIFA Peace Prize , and for giving the inaugural award to United States President Donald Trump.

“There are people who truly care about the future of football — people who aren’t driven by financial interests,” said Klopp. “If someone like that were to step up — if someone like that were to become president — I think that would be a significant improvement.”

“There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it,” he added.

The next election for FIFA president takes place in March 2027. Only former Swiss footballer Ramon Vega and Japan’s Kozo Tashima have announced their intention to run against Infantino.

images.caption: German football coach Jurgen Klopp believes Gianni Infantino has been worse for the game than former chief Sepp Blatter [Maja Hitij/Getty Images]

articles.title: Caso Negreira: llega la hora de la verdad
articles.standfirst: Con la instrucción casi finalizada, la jueza deberá decidir si abre juicio o desestima el caso
articles.summary: Con la instrucción casi finalizada, la jueza deberá decidir si abre juicio o desestima el caso
articles.body: El pasado viernes, Gerard López y Toni Alonso, exentrenador y exdelegado del Barça B, respectivamente, declararon en el Juzgado de Instrucción número 1 de Barcelona por el caso Negreira. Eran las dos últimas personas que quedaban por testificar en esta instrucción, que se encuentra, por tanto, a punto de finalizar, a falta de una documentación que solicitó el Real Madrid y de la digitalización de ciertos documentos. Está previsto que antes de final de año esté completa y ya no habrá más prórrogas, a pesar de los intentos del Real Madrid y de la Fiscalía por alargar la instrucción seis meses más, que fueron denegados por la jueza. A partir de ahora llega el momento clave, en el que la jueza tendrá que decidir si abre juicio oral u opta por el sobreseimiento del caso o de parte de él. Todo dependerá de cómo valore las pruebas que se han recopilado durante los más de tres años y medio que ha durado la instrucción. La jueza se encontrará sobre la mesa con varias certezas que pueden apuntar a los delitos señalados por la Fiscalía, pero también con numerosas incertidumbres y ausencia de pruebas que podrían llevar al cierre del caso sin juicio. Por una parte, existe una serie de hechos que han quedado acreditados a lo largo de esta instrucción, según se indica en una resolución del 10 de octubre de 2023: "Los pagos constatados por la AEAT que fueron realizados por el FC Barcelona y tuvieron como destino las sociedades instrumentales utilizadas por los ENRÍQUEZ, padre e hijo. También está constatado que ENRÍQUEZ padre tenía el cargo de vicepresidente del Comité Técnico de Árbitros de la Real Federación Española de Fútbol. Está constatado que los pagos se realizaron a lo largo de unos 18 años y que fueron incrementándose año tras año. Está constatado que ENRÍQUEZ NEGREIRA dejó de recibir emolumentos del FC Barcelona una vez que cesó en su cargo de vicepresidente del CTA en el año 2018. Está constatado que el investigado ENRÍQUEZ NEGREIRA remitió un burofax al FC Barcelona refiriéndose a la difusión de unas posibles irregularidades de las que aquel tenía conocimiento y que afectarían gravemente al FC Barcelona". A la vista de estos hechos, se presentó una denuncia contra José María Enríquez Negreira, su hijo Javier, el Barcelona, Sandro Rosell, Josep Maria Bartomeu, Albert Soler y Óscar Grau por los siguientes delitos: administración desleal, falsedad en documento mercantil, blanqueo de capitales y corrupción deportiva. La denuncia se refería al pago de 8,4 millones de euros por parte del FC Barcelona, durante 18 años, al entonces vicepresidente del CTA. También se denunció a Laporta, pero este fue exonerado. El argumento de la defensa de los acusados para justificar estos pagos es la existencia de unos informes arbitrales realizados por el hijo de Enríquez Negreira. Se trata de unos dosieres que realmente existen, tal y como se ha demostrado durante la instrucción, ya que se han aportado como prueba varios de ellos en los que se analizaba a los árbitros de la época, como Mateu Lahoz, Undiano Mallenco, Clos Gómez y muchos más. MARCA ha tenido acceso a dicha documentación. La acusación argumenta que ese dinero realmente no se destinaba a esos informes arbitrales, a pesar de que su existencia ha quedado probada. En su lugar, sostiene la teoría de una compra de árbitros por parte del Barcelona o, al menos, de un intento de influir en ellos. No hay ninguna prueba de esas supuestas compras. La Guardia Civil interrogó a más de veinte árbitros y todos ellos negaron este hipotético hecho. También lo hizo Enríquez Negreira, quien declaró en 2021 durante la investigación de Hacienda. Cuando se le preguntó si con el dinero que le daba el Barcelona había pagado a algún árbitro, su respuesta fue tajante: "No". Sin embargo, otra respuesta suya en ese mismo interrogatorio dejó una puerta abierta a la sospecha cuando se le preguntó por el motivo del pago de ese dinero a una de sus sociedades: "Porque así estaban tranquilos de que en el Comité Arbitral no había decisiones en contra del Fútbol Club Barcelona, que todo era neutral". Enríquez Negreira no podrá testificar en el juicio debido a unos problemas de salud mental que han quedado acreditados durante la instrucción. Por tanto, todos los acusados sostienen que los pagos se realizaron por los informes arbitrales. "Todo club de Primera División que no tenga este servicio, algo está haciendo mal", dijo Rosell en su intervención ante el juez. Sobre el hecho de que los entrenadores no los utilizaran, añadió: "Otra cosa es si después lo utilizan. También podemos comprar caterings para 50 jugadores, pero luego solo comen 20; igual que se compran 30 máquinas para el gimnasio y quizá 10 no se usan en la vida. La misión de la Junta es tenerlo todo predispuesto". Ernesto Valverde y Luis Enrique, entrenadores del primer equipo durante el periodo investigado, dijeron que no utilizaban dichos informes y que ni siquiera tenían conocimiento de su existencia. Por su parte, Gerard López, entrenador del filial, aseguró que él sí los utilizaba porque le proporcionaban información relevante sobre los árbitros. Por tanto, está probado que hubo pagos a Enríquez Negreira y a su hijo. Los acusados sostienen que se realizaron por los informes arbitrales, cuya existencia también está probada. Sin embargo, la acusación no comparte esta explicación y argumenta que pudo existir una hipotética compra de partidos, algo para lo que no hay pruebas, o que se pudo favorecer al Barcelona de alguna manera en el ámbito arbitral. Tampoco ha quedado acreditado, salvo por la declaración de Negreira anteriormente mencionada. Y tampoco se sabe dónde acabó el dinero. Negreira lo retiraba poco a poco en efectivo y ahí se pierde el rastro. Es ahora el turno de la jueza.

articles.title: Thomas Frank: How former Spurs boss could restore his reputation and save Crystal Palace
articles.summary: Will Thomas Frank - now confirmed as the new manager of Crystal Palace - rebuild his reputation at Selhurst Park after a bruising time at Tottenham?
articles.body:
"When the time is right I will look forward to my return as a manager, ready to embrace the job with great energy and dedication," said Thomas Frank in June.

That time is now after the Dane was confirmed as the new manager of Crystal Palace , who are two points and a goal difference deficit away from safety at the bottom of the Premier League.

Former boss Pierre Sage was sacked last week after just 16 league and cup games.

The role offers Frank an opportunity to rebuild his reputation after he was sacked by Tottenham in February after eight months.

Frank described it as "an honour" to be "in charge of this fantastic football club" as Palace announced his arrival.

" Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League," Frank told Palace's website.

"I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them."

Palace chairman Steve Parish said Frank was the "perfect fit for our club".

But how big is the challenge at Selhurst Park that awaits the man who made his name at Brentford ?

"It's going to be a bit of a shock for Thomas Frank," former West Ham and England goalkeeper Rob Green tells BBC Sport.

"He had his success at Brentford - a very well-run club where players are brought in with a lot of thinking and planning to take over the players they sell for profit.

"That doesn't happen at Crystal Palace .

"They lose players and then have a mad scramble to get players in. They have a team that has been decimated by sales and not replaced by the same quality.

"Thomas Frank needs to find something within that team that builds and garners the belief that means that they can compete in the Premier League, because it feels a long way short of that right now."

Will Frank prove the right fit for Palace and haul the Eagles out of the relegation zone?

Since getting the sack at Tottenham after 26 league games last season, Frank has been out of management longer than he was in charge of Spurs .

In the summer he released a statement in which he said "there have been conversations and opportunities" to return to management, but that he had "decided not to rush into the next role".

Frank's name was heavily linked with Palace before they went for a head coach with no Premier League experience to replace Oliver Glasner - the man who delivered an FA Cup, a Conference League title and Community Shield before moving to Nottingham Forest .

"Palace had one of the best managers they have had, if not forever, silverware coming across the doorstep. Look at what they achieved last season and instead of building on that, they dismantled a team," said former Tottenham and England goalkeeper Paul Robinson.

Frank once described managing as being on a "hamster wheel" and a "crazy circus". , external

HIs coaching staff will include current assistant manager Paddy McCarthy and goalkeeping coach Andy Quy, who previously worked with him at Brentford .

So why does he feel now is the right moment to return to management at a club propping up the table?

Frank, who was part of BBC Sport's World Cup punditry team during the summer, will be coming into the job refreshed and with renewed energy and enthusiasm following several months out of the game.

Between his appointment as Brentford boss in October 2018 and the sack at Tottenham earlier this year, he managed without a break for seven years and four months.

Spending the past few months away from Premier League pressure has allowed Frank, in his own words, to "study, observe and learn from other leaders both within sport and beyond".

Will his positivity and passion rub off on a Palace team who have lost seven times in 10 top-flight matches?

Frank, who places a major emphasis on set-piece organisation, will have to hit the ground running at Palace, who have lost their past four league games.

They have conceded more goals than anyone else in the Premier League (24) and have scored only 10 themselves.

"If you want someone to go in and restore some stability and defensive solidity while improving the set-piece element of the team, then Thomas Frank is the perfect man for the job," Times football writer Tom Allnutt told BBC Radio 5 Live's Football Daily podcast.

With the Premier League season just 10 games old, Frank certainly has time to turn it around and will have targets in mind when the transfer window opens in January.

Palace sold France centre-back Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea for £52m and Colombia right-back Daniel Munoz to Nottingham Forest for £22m during the summer transfer window.

Allnutt added: "We know they have sold so many good players and so far I don't think they have really replaced them adequately."

Another challenge for Frank is getting midfielder Adam Wharton, who has not played for England since March, back to something like his best form.

These are all challenges the new manager will relish.

After his bruising experience at Tottenham - having established Brentford in the Premier League - Frank has decided to climb back on the hamster wheel with Palace.

" Crystal Palace and Thomas Frank feels like a very good fit," added Robinson.

Thomas Frank has a lot of work to do as Crystal Palace have undoubtedly been the worst team in the Premier League so far this season, ranking bottom not just in points (seven) but also goal difference (-14) and expected goal difference (-8.1).

It's the defence where Frank will have to focus most of his attention. Not only have Palace conceded the most goals (24) but they've also faced the most shots (189) and have the worst expected goals against (xGA) figure in the league (21.9).

Their attack has actually not been too bad. While only Hull have taken fewer shots, the Eagles have created really good chances and have perhaps been unlucky not to score a few more goals given the opportunities they've had.

There is also one significant factor in Frank's favour. Although Palace may be bottom of the Premier League, they are certainly not cut adrift as they sit just two points from safety.

The side propping up the table at this stage have had an average of just three points in the past 10 seasons, but for as bad as they've been, Palace have seven - the most the bottom side have had after 10 games for 24 years.

articles.title: Bill Belichick Reacts to Fight Caught on Video After UNC's Loss to Louisville, ACC Issues Punishment
articles.summary: UNC head coach Bill Belichick was forced to step in when some Tar Heels players got into it with Louisville's players following Saturday's 16-14 loss.
articles.body:
UNC head coach Bill Belichick was forced to step in when some Tar Heels players got into it with Louisville's players following Saturday's 16-14 loss.

After the game, Belichick made it clear that he wasn't pleased with his players' involvement in the brawl.

"You play the game between the whistles. That's not what we're here for," Belichick said, per Bryan Logan of ClutchPoints. "We got out there and got everybody out as quickly as possible."

The ACC announced Monday that it has issued fines and suspensions to both North Carolina and Louisville in accordance with the conference's Sportsmanship Policy.

Tensions ran high for UNC after they fought back without starting quarterback Billy Edwards Jr., who was injured in the second half. After scoring a touchdown in the fourth quarter to make it a two-point game and forcing a punt, the Tar Heels' day ended when backup quarterback Travis Burgess threw a game-sealing interception.

Belichick was at midfield to shake hands with Louisville quarterback Lincoln Kienholz and coach Jeff Brohm when the brawl broke out. Brohm also lamented the post-game fireworks.

"It's obviously unfortunate," Louisville coach Jeff Brohm said. "You try to get things broken up as fast as you can. It didn't get broken up too fast. But you never want to see that happen. So I'd have to see what really started it. Hopefully we can correct that and not do that again."

UNC linebacker Derek McDonald added, "We should've won between the whistles. None of that needs to happen. Unnecessary."

After falling to 5-5, Belichick and the Tar Heels will try to bounce back when they face Virginia (5-5) in another ACC matchup next Saturday.

articles.title: José Bernabéu, elegido por unanimidad presidente de la Federación de Peñas del Sureste
articles.standfirst: La entidad agrupa a 61 peñas madridistas de Castellón, Valencia, Alicante, Albacete y Murcia
articles.summary: La entidad agrupa a 61 peñas madridistas de Castellón, Valencia, Alicante, Albacete y Murcia
articles.body: José Bernabéu ha sido elegido por unanimidad presidente de la Federación de Peñas del Sureste en la asamblea celebrada el pasado fin de semana. La entidad reúne a 61 peñas del Real Madrid repartidas entre las provincias de Castellón, Valencia, Alicante, Albacete y Murcia. La elección contó con el respaldo unánime de las peñas asistentes y sitúa a Bernabéu al frente de una federación que conecta al movimiento peñista madridista de estas cinco provincias. Tras su nombramiento, el nuevo presidente señaló la colaboración entre las peñas y la unidad como las bases del trabajo que pretende desarrollar al frente de la entidad. Bernabéu agradeció la confianza recibida y trasladó su intención de impulsar el proyecto con la participación de las agrupaciones que integran la federación.

articles.title: Philippe Diallo, el candidato de la UEFA para hacer frente a Infantino: del boxeo y el fútbol a los despachos
articles.standfirst: El organismo europeo ha anunciado el nombre del presidente de la Federación Francesa de Fútbol para presentarse a las elecciones a la presidencia de FIFA el próximo mes de marzo
articles.summary: El organismo europeo ha anunciado el nombre del presidente de la Federación Francesa de Fútbol para presentarse a las elecciones a la presidencia de FIFA el próximo mes de marzo
articles.body: En una reunión celebrada hoy y presidida por el presidente de la UEFA, Aleksander Ceferin, las federaciones nacionales representadas en el Comité Ejecutivo de la UEFA y en el Consejo de la FIFA invitaron a Philippe Diallo, presidente de la Federación Francesa de Fútbol (FFF), a presentarse como candidato a las elecciones presidenciales de la FIFA que se celebrarán en marzo de 2027 y le brindaron por unanimidad su pleno apoyo", acaba de comunicar la UEFA. Concluye así el misterio después de meses de búsqueda por parte de la UEFA en la que han aparecido varios nombres, entre ellos el de Arsène Wenger, que finalmente no ha aceptado la propuesta y seguirá en principio desempeñando sus funciones como director de Desarrollo Mundial del Fútbol de FIFA. La candidatura de Diallo debe ser ratificada oficialmente por el comité ejecutivo de la propia Federación Francesa de Fútbol antes de que cierre el plazo de inscripción de la FIFA el miércoles 18 de noviembre, tres meses antes del Congreso de la FIFA donde se celebran las elecciones en Rabat. UEFA y Concacaf han ido de la mano estos meses en la búsqueda de un candidato. De hecho, uno de los primeros nombres que sonó con fuerza fue el de Victor Montagliani, actual presidente de esa confederación. La idea era que no fuera europeo, pero al final se ha ido estrechando la búsqueda hasta dar con Diallo. “Philippe Diallo cuenta con una amplia experiencia en todos los niveles del fútbol: ha dirigido la organización que representa a los clubes de fútbol profesional francés, ha formado parte de la junta directiva de la liga profesional francesa y ha participado en las estructuras de resolución de disputas de la FIFA, antes de convertirse en presidente de la FFF y miembro del Comité Ejecutivo de la UEFA en 2023”, apunta la UEFA en su comunicado. "Ante la profunda preocupación por el rumbo que está tomando la FIFA, las asociaciones nacionales han abogado por recuperar la unidad y la confianza dentro de la comunidad futbolística mundial. Asimismo, han reclamado una FIFA que sitúe el desarrollo del fútbol en todas las regiones del mundo en el centro de su misión, que mantenga los más altos estándares de gobernanza y que trabaje en estrecha colaboración con sus asociaciones miembro, confederaciones y demás agentes del fútbol. Asimismo, han manifestado su plena confianza en que Philippe Diallo aportará el liderazgo necesario para alcanzar este objetivo”, concluye UEFA. En sus años de juventud, Diallo trata de seguir los pasos de su padre, ex boxeador. Es hijo de Souleymane Diallo (1937-2024), boxeador franco-senegalés apodado «la Pantera del ring». Tres veces campeón de Francia de peso medio en la década de 1960 y subcampeón de Europa en 1964, su padre le inculcó desde muy temprana edad la cultura del deporte de competición. El presidente de la FFF lo intentó también con el fútbol y se enrola en la cantera del Nantes. Era un centrocampista ofensivo bajo la dirección de entrenadores como Raynald Denoueix y Jean-Claude Suaudeau. Sin embargo, años después decide volcarse en los estudios y hace derecho. Tras acabar la carrera ingresa en el Instituto de Estudios Políticos de París (Sciences Po). En una época en la que las profesiones relacionadas con la gestión deportiva aún no estaban muy extendidas entre los titulados de las grandes escuelas, su doble perfil como jurista y exjugador formado en un club le abrió finalmente las puertas de la Unión de Clubes Profesionales de Fútbol (UCPF) en 1992, a la edad de 29 años. Zinedine Zidane acaba de colocar a Francia en los cuartos de la Liga de Naciones. Diallo fue uno de los artífices de este desembarco. Entendió que era la persona ideal porque Didier Deschamps no iba a renovar su contrato. Aterriza en la FFF en marzo de 2021 en la lista de Noël Le Graët como tesorero general, después vicepresidente delegado, situándose como la mano derecha del presidente. Llegan los momentos de crisis en la presidencia de la Federación a raíz de las polémicas y del informe de auditoría ministerial que apuntaba a Noël Le Graët y a la directora general Florence Hardouin. Philippe Diallo asume entonces la presidencia interina el 11 de enero de 2023 y tras la dimisión definitiva de Noël Le Graët, es elegido presidente el 10 de junio de 2023 con el 91 % de los votos para completar el mandato en curso.

articles.title: England have golden opportunity to win Euro 2028, says Martin Tyler as legendary commentator reflects on 50-year career
articles.summary: Martin Tyler's new book 'Tales from the Gantry: Letters from a Lifetime in Football' was published on Monday; the legendary ex-Sky Sports commentator has backed England to win their first major trophy since 1966 at the 2028 Euros on home soil after Sunday's 3-2 Nations League win in Spain
articles.body:
The legendary football commentator, whose new book 'Tales from the Gantry: Letters from a Lifetime in Football' was published on Monday, knows a thing or two about England teams, good and bad, having called over 350 Three Lions internationals while attending an astonishing 13 World Cup finals during a decorated 53-year career that is still going today.

The book is "historical", says Tyler. "It is what I was thinking about in football that week. There's 110 different essays, half a dozen of them were letters from America.

"I wrote 500 words a week for two and a half years. It starts early in 2004 and finishes in July 2026."

Tyler's illustrious career began back in December 1974 commentating for ITV region Southern Television, then Yorkshire Television and Granada, while he was chosen to call the 1982 World Cup final alongside Ian St John before joining BSkyB [the sports arm of which became Sky Sports in 1991] in 1990.

And it was there where for the next 33 years, he became the voice of football for so many, commentating on many of the most unforgettable and dramatic games in that time.

"It'll be 52 years in December," Tyler recalls, almost himself taken aback by the longevity of his career.

"It's extraordinary, really. Talk about time going fast when you're having fun and I've had a lot of fun. Time has gone very fast!

"Then the Premier League came along and the rest is history…."

Undoubtedly, Tyler's most memorable piece of Premier League commentary came at the Etihad Stadium in May 2012 when Manchester City scored twice in stoppage time to be crowned champions for the first time in 44 years after beating Queen's Park Rangers to win the Premier League on goal difference from arch-rivals Manchester United.

"AGUEROOOOO!" Tyler exclaimed as the Argentine's late strike hit the net to send the Etihad into delirium. "I swear you'll never see anything like this ever again! So, watch it, drink it in."

Looking back now, Tyler is happy with how one of the most played pieces of football commentary in this country came out.

"I think my statement still holds good and basically, it's the football you respond to, we don't create anything as commentators, we react to it, it's a reactive job and we try and find the right words at the right time," he says.

"And sometimes you do, and sometimes you don't, and when I think about that particular game you're referring to, it might have been a different story if I hadn't come up with the words, but I managed to do it, it was one of my good days."

Speaking of good days, well that is exactly what England had in the Spanish capital on Sunday night as the visitors inflicted a first defeat on the world and European champions in two years and 43 matches in what Tyler labelled a near-faultless display.

"That was a very impressive England performance," he says. "For an hour, it was almost perfection. And then, of course, it became what 11 against 10 should be, but isn't always. To be fair to Spain, they came up with some really important questions that England had to deal with."

One player in particular caught Tyler's eye at the Wanda Metropolitano.

"We talk a lot about Old Trafford, we should be talking about young Trafford now," he added. "I think that will be seen as the day where he announced whether he would replace Jordan Pickford as a fine goalkeeper.

"Immediately, I don't know, but he has proved that he is capable of being England's No 1 as Jordan's career will, obviously, because of the difference in age, will not exactly peter out, because he won't let that happen.

"But he will realise that there's some serious competition and that's what happens in life, you know. You have your run, and then somebody comes and says, 'I'll have a bit of that' and undoubtedly, England wouldn't have won the game without him."

In fact, so impressive were England for an hour in Madrid that Tyler feels he is now not far away from the thrill of commentating on England finally getting their hands on a major piece of silverware for the first time since 1966.

"I would love to do that," he says. "The best I can do is the under-18s when Gary Neville was playing, back in 1993, which we covered on Sky Sports. So that's as close as I've come.

"I've seen England go out at pretty much every World Cup since anyone can remember really. I've certainly seen England go out, even in 1954, 1962 and 1966 as a television watcher, although I went to a game in '66.

"And 1970, I remember walking out, I was still living with my parents, into the streets going, 'how did we manage to lose that?' We were the holders, which made it even more painful!

"England are looking capable of winning. I really hope that they can win the Nations League because I rate the Nations League as a tournament. England came, we forget, third in the first one.

"I can't honestly say looking at that first half last night, I can't believe that any international team in the world would have coped with that kind of performance.

"That was top of the range and the way in modern football where press is everything, they squeeze the life out of the world champions. It didn't win them the match as such because of what happened afterwards, they needed other elements like James Trafford to make sure we did win the game, but it's exciting times for England.

"The expression is you can't win them all, but it would be nice to win one. I'm sure we will. I'm really convinced. Last night, I was watching and I thought, 'this team will win something' and that's obviously a golden opportunity coming up here in the next Euros."

Tyler, now 81, still hopes to be commentating on the European championship in 2028 when he may finally get that chance to describe England captain Harry Kane walking up the Wembley steps to lift the Henri Delaunay Trophy.

"As you get older, I would say this to everybody past a certain age, don't retire," he says. "Keep things in your life!"

And what better way to hang up the microphone after more than half a century commentating than to call England's major trophy win for 62 years.

articles.title: Wales Nations League: Neco Williams ruled out of Portugal game
articles.summary: Wales will be without right-back Neco Williams for their final Nations League group match against Portugal, while goalkeeper Karl Darlow is a doubt.
articles.body:
Wales will be without right-back Neco Williams for their final Nations League group match against reigning champions Portugal on Tuesday (19:45 GMT), while goalkeeper Karl Darlow is a doubt.

Nottingham Forest's Williams has been ruled out after he was injured during Saturday's 3-1 defeat in Norway, while Manchester United's Darlow missed training on Monday and will be assessed further.

Midfielder Ethan Ampadu will also miss out at Cardiff City Stadium because of suspension, but centre-back Ben Cabango and winger Sorba Thomas are available after serving one-match bans.

Wales will finish bottom of Group A4 whatever happens against leaders Portugal, and Craig Bellamy's side will have a relegation play-off in March against one of the League B runners-up for a place in the top tier.

"One or two players had to come off through injury [in Norway]. One or two have come through; one or two haven't," said Bellamy.

"Neco's going to be out. Darlow, we'll wait and see later, and everyone else is fully fit."

What Wales need to stay in Nations League top tier

With less riding on this fixture than there might have been, Bellamy could be tempted to make further changes to his side from the loss in Oslo.

Cardiff City attacking midfielder Rubin Colwill shone as a substitute, while Bournemouth's David Brooks came off the bench to score an excellent goal.

Colwill's performance was a particularly popular talking point among fans, many of whom have long been calling for the 24-year-old playmaker to feature more regularly for Wales.

"Rubin's been pushing [to start] for a while," said Bellamy. "Once you get this kid in the final third, then he's a player. We've just got to get him in those areas.

"But he's also got to offer us without the ball as well. If you're not good without the ball, you cannot be a top player.

"If you want a lesson tomorrow without the ball, watch Vitinha [Portugal's Paris St-Germain midfielder] if he plays.

"Rubin has moved [up a level] and long may that continue, because if it does Wales have got a brilliant player.

"I'm more harsh on Rubin because I've known him since he was so young, but credit to him and his manager at Cardiff [Brian Barry-Murphy].

"He's helping develop a real player for us that's going to hopefully have a huge impact for the next five to 10 years."

articles.summary: Pubill terminó lesionada ante Inglaterra, Cuti todavía recuperándose y Le Normand es el único que está sano
articles.body: Buenas noticias para el Atlético. David Hancko ha sido liberado por el seleccionador de Eslovaquia para el choque que se disputa hoy lunes ante Kazajistán tras jugar el partido completo ante Islas Feroes... que acabó con empate a dos. La lesión de Pubill ante Inglaterra deja coja una posición en la que todavía se está esperando a Cuti Romero, que avanza en su recuperación para poder estar disponible ante el Getafe el próximo domingo. Al menos, El Cholo tendrá disponible a Hancko así como a un Le Normand que es de los seis futbolistas que se quedaron en Madrid trabajando la pasada semana en las sesiones de miércoles, jueves y viernes. El rol de Hancko, como ya pasó la temporada pasada, está siendo el de intocable. Único central zurdo puro, ha formado pareja con los otros tres centrales: Cuti, Pubill y Le Normand. Con la decisión del seleccionador Vladimír Weiss,, también estará listo para incorporarse desde mañana a la disciplina rojiblanca.

articles.title: Las pruebas descartan una lesión grave de Pubill: tiene un esguince leve
articles.standfirst: El central se retiró lesionado ante Inglaterra en el minuto 20
articles.summary: El central se retiró lesionado ante Inglaterra en el minuto 20
articles.body: Buenas noticias para el Atlético. Marc Pubill no está lesionado de consideración al descartar las pruebas realizadas hoy una dolencia importante. El central rojiblanco, así las cosas, sufre un esguince leve provocado en los primeros minutos del choque ante Inglaterra del domingo. El jugador, en cualquier caso, se someterá a tratamiento los próximos días para perderse los menos partidos posibles. Es complicado que llegue al choque ante el Getafe del domingo, pero la satisfacción es evidente porque en primera instancia se temió por una dolencia mayor. Hay que recordar que Pubill es uno de los jugadores importantes en la rotación del Atlético. De central o de lateral derecho, el ex del Almería es clave para Simeone, que le ha utilizado en 14 partidos esta temporada. Con el calendario más que cargado (hay nueve partidos desde el domingo hasta antes de Navidad), tener disponible a Pubill será fundamental para el entrenador argentino.

articles.title: La Federación estudia acciones legales tras una condena a pagar más de 700.000 euros por un contrato de la anterior gestión
articles.standfirst: El acuerdo contemplaba una contraprestación superior a 1,6 millones y tenía como objeto la creación de un medio destinado a difundir noticias sobre la candidatura de España para organizar el Mundial de 2030
articles.summary: El acuerdo contemplaba una contraprestación superior a 1,6 millones y tenía como objeto la creación de un medio destinado a difundir noticias sobre la candidatura de España para organizar el Mundial de 2030
articles.body: La Junta Directiva de la Federación Española de Fútbol ha encargado a sus servicios jurídicos que estudien posibles acciones legales tras conocer una resolución judicial que obliga a la institución a pagar más de 700.000 euros por un contrato firmado por los anteriores gestores en 2022. Según ha informado la RFEF, el acuerdo contemplaba una contraprestación total superior a 1,6 millones de euros y tenía como objeto la creación de un medio de comunicación destinado, presuntamente, a difundir noticias sobre la candidatura de España para organizar el Mundial de 2030. La actual Junta Directiva sostiene, sin embargo, que ese medio publicó numerosos artículos con ataques a distintos organismos cuyos intereses diferían de los de la presidencia y la gestión federativa de aquella etapa. La Federación ha expresado su condena y repulsa ante estos hechos y considera que han causado un grave perjuicio económico a la institución. Por ello, ha encomendado de forma inmediata a sus servicios jurídicos un análisis de las actuaciones que puede emprender. La RFEF no descarta acudir a ninguna vía judicial para defender los intereses de la entidad y depurar las posibles responsabilidades derivadas de este contrato o de otros asuntos en los que se detecte mala praxis.

articles.title: Dolores Aveiro: "Le engañaron, ni siquiera sus compañeros le han respetado"
articles.standfirst: La madre de Cristiano habla sobre el homenaje de Portugal a su hijo tras su retirada de la selección
articles.summary: La madre de Cristiano habla sobre el homenaje de Portugal a su hijo tras su retirada de la selección
articles.body: Dolores Aveiro, madre de Cristiano Ronaldo, habló en los micrófonos de SIC Noticias tras el homenaje que la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol le dedicó a su hijo. Dolores expresó el dolor que sentía tras la retirada de Cristiano y valoró el comportamiento de sus compañeros de selección. "Me entristeció que le engañaran y todavía estoy triste. Fue una derrota (la de Portugal ante Dinamarca) y estuvo bien merecida; me alegré. El homenaje debería haberse hecho delante de él, no en su ausencia. El homenaje se va a celebrar aquí, en el Sporting", aseguró la madre de Ronaldo. "No, sus compañeros de selección no han mostrado cariño y respeto. Él (Cristiano) también lo siente así. No se le ha respetado, ni siquiera sus compañeros", concluyó una Dolores visiblemente enfadada.

articles.title: UEFA backs France’s Philippe Diallo to challenge Infantino in FIFA election
articles.summary: French Football Federation chief Diallo emerges as a strong challenger in FIFA’s upcoming presidential election.
articles.body:
European football’s governing body UEFA has given its “unanimous” backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election.

UEFA invited Diallo to “stand as a candidate in the FIFA presidential election in March 2027”, the continental body said in a statement on Monday, adding that European national associations had “unanimously pledged their full support”.

The deadline for rival candidates to declare themselves is Wednesday, November 18.

The Union of European Football Associations (UEFA), which boasts 55 member associations, said Diallo “has accepted the invitation to stand” and that his candidature is set to be confirmed at a meeting of the French Football Federation (FFF) on Tuesday.

Diallo, the 63-year-old son of a Senegalese boxing champion, has been president of the FFF since January 2023.

He was initially appointed to the post on an interim basis when previous chief Noel Le Graet was forced to stand down following a series of controversies.

Diallo, from Saint-Nazaire on France’s Atlantic coast, was then elected to the role by a large majority in June of that year, before being re-elected in December 2024 for a new four-year term.

Under its Slovenian president Aleksander Ceferin, UEFA has led the opposition to Infantino since his announcement in late July of a project to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino quickly abandoned the proposal in the face of widespread uproar, but UEFA has since gone to court in the US state of Florida in an attempt to gather evidence for a potential complaint of “criminal mismanagement” against the FIFA president in Switzerland.

UEFA had been struggling to find a credible candidate to stand against Infantino in the election, which will take place at the FIFA Congress on March 18 next year in the Moroccan capital, Rabat.

Confederation of North, Central American and Caribbean Association Football (CONCACAF) chief Victor Montagliani had been mooted as a candidate, but the Canadian later announced his desire to stand for a new term as the head of his confederation.

The Asian Football Confederation, which consists of 47 member associations, announced last month that it was backing Infantino for re-election.

Diallo said in September that the FFF was withdrawing its backing for Infantino in the election.

“We believe that the trust placed in the FIFA president has been betrayed, and that the way in which the governance of world football is envisaged no longer reflects us,” he said at the time.

Infantino, a former UEFA secretary general, has been in charge of FIFA since 2016.

articles.title: A Raphinha le caen palos por todos lados
articles.standfirst: Desde Brasil y desde Barcelona
articles.summary: Desde Brasil y desde Barcelona
articles.body: Raphinha se ha situado sin querer en el centro de una polémica. Se ha convertido en el objetivo de los más radicales, tanto en Brasil como en Barcelona. El motivo es la selección brasileña, su presencia o su ausencia, según se quiera mirar. Es cierto que el futbolista se lesionó en las tres convocatorias anteriores de su selección. Y es probable que Raphinha pudiera haber hecho algo más para evitar alguna de esas lesiones. Este fue el punto de partida para recibir críticas desde Barcelona, algunas muy duras. El segundo capítulo tuvo lugar en Brasil. El delantero, a la vista de esas lesiones anteriores, habló con Ancelotti para dosificar sus minutos en esta convocatoria. Y llegaron a un pacto. Bien hecho. Sin embargo, a raíz de este acuerdo, comenzaron las críticas en su país, argumentando que no sentía la camiseta de Brasil. Raphinha tuvo que salir en rueda de prensa y, entre lágrimas, explicar los motivos de esa reunión con el seleccionador. Aseguró que amaba su camiseta y que lo único que quería era estar disponible tanto para el Barcelona como para Brasil. El último capítulo se ha vivido este fin de semana. Raphinha fue expulsado en el partido frente a Japón y no jugará el siguiente encuentro. Se especuló con su regreso a la Ciudad Condal para ponerse a las órdenes de Flick, pero al final se quedó en la convocatoria. Nuevas críticas, otra vez desde Barcelona, por no regresar de inmediato. Si lo hubiera hecho, todo Brasil se habría puesto en su contra por 'dejar tirado' al equipo. Un capitán, Raphinha estaba estrenando esta condición, no abandona el barco. Sean cuales sean las circunstancias, se queda hasta el final, y eso es lo que hizo, con buen criterio. Da un poco de pena ver cómo están tratando a un jugador que siempre ha sido modélico. Si de algo no se puede acusar a Raphinha en ningún momento es de falta de compromiso. Ni con la selección ni con el Barcelona.

articles.title: Thomas Frank: Crystal Palace appoint former Spurs and Brentford boss as Pierre Sage's successor at Selhurst Park
articles.summary: Thomas Frank returns to the Premier League with Crystal Palace after being sacked by Tottenham in February; he will replace Pierre Sage at Selhurst Park; Palace are bottom of the table with just seven points from their first 10 games
articles.body:
The Dane replaces Pierre Sage, who was dismissed on November 12 following a seventh league defeat of the season to Liverpool.

Frank has signed a deal until the summer of 2029 - and took charge of his first training session as Palace boss on Monday.

Palace chairman Steve Parish said of Frank: "He has a proven track record of both creating winning teams and improving players making him the perfect fit for our club.

"I'm confident Thomas' extensive experience in the Premier League will help us achieve our goals for the rest of the season."

Frank was among a list of names that Palace considered in the summer before Sage was appointed to the role.

Other candidates that Palace were interested in included Frank Lampard , Sean Dyche , Vitor Pereira , Kim Hellberg , Vitor Matos, Tony Popovic, Jens Berthel Askou and Ole Werner.

Frank added: "It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic Football Club. I'm really, really looking forward to it.

"Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them."

Frank had great success at Brentford during his seven-year spell between 2018 and 2025, getting the Bees into the Premier League and then establishing them as a top-flight club, reaching a ninth-place finish in 2023.

He then moved to Tottenham last season to replace Ange Postecoglou, but was sacked after less than eight months in charge with the club in 16th place, five points above the relegation zone.

Spurs only sealed survival from relegation on the final day of last season, by which stage Roberto De Zerbi was head coach.

Frank failed to win over the Tottenham faithful, with his short tenure littered with setbacks, including drinking from a coffee cup which carried the badge of rivals Arsenal.

Palace are bottom of the Premier League with seven points, two from safety. They face the team in 17th place - Coventry - when the league resumes on Saturday.

They are also 21st in the Europa League table - which would currently see them through to the knockout play-off phase - with one win, two draws and one loss so far. The Eagles face Real Sociedad - a place ahead of them on goal difference - at Selhurst Park in their next European fixture on November 26.

Frank was Crystal Palace's No 1 choice to take over from Sage.

Palace believe their squad is much better than their current position in the Premier League table.

Frank is believed to be rejuvenated and refreshed after taking some time away from the game, having recently returned from Australia.

His first task is to get Palace out of the relegation zone, with the club two points from safety.

The Dane's willingness to use a variety of formations could be a key factor in bringing the best out of Palace's current squad.

Frank was also interviewed for the Manchester United and Chelsea jobs in the summer of 2024.

Who will be part of Frank's backroom staff?

Two members of Frank's backroom team have already been announced.

Current assistant manager Paddy McCarthy is staying on, alongside goalkeeper coach Andy Quy , who coincidentally worked with Frank at Brentford.

However, Palace are working on putting together Frank's coaching team.

They are approaching Chelsea to get Bernardo Cueva . He was a set-piece coach under Frank at Brentford before moving to Chelsea - but Cueva would work as a coach at Palace.

Palace also want to add Justin Cochrane to Frank's coaching team. The two worked together at Brentford and Spurs and Cochrane is currently part of Thomas Tuchel's England coaching team.

Frank also wants Chris Haslam to join Palace with him. Haslam was a fitness and performance coach for 14 years at Brentford, and then performance and assistant coach under Frank at Tottenham.
