articles.title: McShay Drops Honest Take on Arch Manning, Sam Leavitt's NFL Draft Stock After Struggles in Texas-LSU
articles.summary: Saturday's game between Texas and LSU wasn't exactly a coming-out party for quarterbacks Arch Manning and Sam Leavitt, and one expert had a blunt assessment of both of them.
articles.body:
Saturday's game between Texas and LSU wasn't exactly a coming-out party for quarterbacks Arch Manning and Sam Leavitt, and one expert had a blunt assessment of both of them.

During Monday's episode of The McShay Show (15:20 mark), NFL draft guru Todd McShay suggested that Manning and Leavitt would benefit from forgoing the 2027 NFL draft and spending another year in college.

"Arch Manning and Sam Leavitt project still in my book to be dynamic quarterbacks that have a path to be good starters in the NFL and can win a ton of games in the NFL and can possibly win a Super Bowl in the NFL. They have the physical tools and enough instinct and playmaking skills to them that they can be that," McShay said. "But I also thank god for both of them; they have another year of college, because neither is ready for the NFL right now."

Manning threw a last-second touchdown pass to lead the Longhorns to a 22-21 win over the Tigers, but that wasn't enough to overlook his struggles on Saturday. He finished with just 174 yards and threw three interceptions on 19-of-35 passing. He also tied for the team lead with 35 rushing yards and added another score on the ground.

Leavitt wasn't much better, going 27-of-37 for 244 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions as LSU fell to 6-4 this season.

In the latest mock draft by B/R's NFL Scouting Department, Manning was still projected to be selected fourth overall by the New York Jets. However, Leavitt wasn't projected as a first-round selection.

At this point, it wouldn't be a surprise if Manning and Leavitt use their final year of college eligibility to continue to hone their skills before making the jump to the NFL in 2028.

articles.title: El Madrid más 'extremo' en los fichajes
articles.standfirst: Diomande, JJ Gabriel, Ciria... El club ha convertido el talento de banda en una obsesión que recorre toda su estructura, del primer equipo al último escalón de La Fábrica
articles.summary: Diomande, JJ Gabriel, Ciria... El club ha convertido el talento de banda en una obsesión que recorre toda su estructura, del primer equipo al último escalón de La Fábrica
articles.body: Hay una posición que el Real Madrid ha decidido blindar a todos los niveles, y no es la portería ni el eje de la defensa. Es la banda. En apenas un año, el club ha reunido una cantidad llamativa de futbolistas que comparten un mismo rasgo —desequilibrar en el uno contra uno— y los ha repartido por cada escalón de su organigrama, desde el césped del Bernabéu hasta los juveniles de Valdebebas. La apuesta es acumular extremos, y acumularlos jóvenes. El ejemplo más caro llegó en agosto. Yan Diomande, extremo costamarfileño nacido en 2006, aterrizó procedente del RB Leipzig en una operación que rondó los 140 millones de euros entre fijos y variables, lo que lo convierte en el fichaje más caro de la historia del club. Y, lejos de necesitar un periodo de adaptación, se ha asentado de forma relámpago, desbancando a Vinicius en el extremo izquierdo del Madrid. Ya acumula cuatro goles, tres de ellos de bella factura y que han dado rédito a los blancos. El siguiente en aterrizar será JJ Gabriel, cuestión de semanas, según informó este diario. El inglés, que acaba de cumplir 16 años, llega del Manchester United en una operación de repercusión internacional, disputada con varios grandes de Europa, y fue protagonista por sus declaraciones en exclusiva a MARCA: “Mi sueño es ganar el Balón de Oro”. Puede actuar como mediapunta, pero su físico y sus virtudes invitan a imaginarlo como extremo izquierdo, un recorrido que ya siguió en su día Vinicius. Valdebebas es donde la tendencia se vuelve sistema. Ahí la lista se multiplica. El verano dejó a Sergio Castellón (2008), reclutado del Rayo Vallecano para el Juvenil A pese al interés de Barça y Atlético: zurdo imaginativo, capaz de jugar en las dos bandas y por dentro y que es el tercer máximo goleador del primer juvenil blanco con cinco goles. También a Raúl Lema (2010), extremo zurdo internacional en las categorías inferiores de España, que llegó desde el Deportivo de La Coruña tras foguearse por encima de su edad. Meses antes, en enero de 2026, el club había sumado a Iker Doblas (2007), procedente de la DAMM y antes del L’Hospitalet, que ha ido ascendiendo en la estructura hasta el Real Madrid C. El caso con más frutos de ese grupo es Alexis Ciria (Badajoz, 2008). Llegó del Sevilla en enero, extremo izquierdo con galones de delantero, regateador y creativo. Su debut en pretemporada con el primer equipo fue toda una carta de presentación —una rabona y un gol ante la Fiorentina, con elogios públicos de Mourinho—, y el tramo final del curso pasado lo cerró con tres goles y una asistencia en apenas 275 minutos con el Castilla. Ciria arrancó en el Juvenil A, ascendió al Madrid C y acabó la temporada en el primer filial blanco, donde ya está instalado. Su espectacular impacto está directamente relacionado con los históricos cuatro títulos logrados por el Juvenil A: Youth, Liga, Copa de Campeones e Intercontinental sub 20. Llegó de puntillas y ya tiene un valor de mercado de un millón de euros, siendo todavía juvenil. A ese bloque internacional se suma Clifford Nana, extremo ghanés de 16 años que pasó por La Masia entre 2019 y 2022 antes de recalar, vía DAMM, en el Juvenil C, una muestra de cómo el Madrid rastrea talento de banda más allá de las fronteras. En esa misma red de captación internacional se inscribe Lawrence Osayende, extremo izquierdo nacido presuntamente en 2012 y llegado del Santutxu, al que se ha situado en el Cadete B: la apuesta por el desequilibrio desciende hasta los peldaños más bajos del organigrama. La apuesta, además, no parte de cero. La Fábrica ya atesoraba perfiles de ese corte, y conviene no verlos como novedades, sino como el caldo de cultivo que explica la estrategia. Daniel Yáñez (Cádiz, 2007), extremo diestro a pierna cambiada, debutó con el primer equipo en diciembre de 2024, milita en el Castilla y fue una de las figuras de la Youth League conquistada en 2026. Gabri Valero (Menorca, 2007), formado en Valdebebas y hoy en el Real Madrid C, levantó esa misma Youth League y la Copa de Campeones. Adri Pérez (Marbella, 2008), extremo izquierdo internacional sub-18, destaca por su olfato goleador a pierna cambiada en el Juvenil A. Álvaro Leiva, extremo zurdo llegado del Algeciras en 2022, ya debutó con el primer equipo y este verano optó por quedarse en el Castilla para pelear por su sitio pese a tener opciones de salida. Y a ellos se asoma Rubén López (Madrid, 2008), formado en La Fábrica con una etapa en el Rayo Vallecano y hoy en el Juvenil A, al que el club encuadra como centrocampista pero cuya polivalencia ofensiva lo acerca a ese perfil de jugador capaz de aparecer también por fuera.

articles.title: Slegers praises Arsenal’s dedication and effort despite frustrating draw with London City Lionesses
articles.summary: Arsenal head coach Renée Slegers was pleased with her side’s performance despite being held to a frustrating 1-1 draw by London City Lionesses on Sunday.Frid...
articles.body:
Arsenal head coach Renée Slegers was pleased with her side's performance despite being held to a frustrating 1-1 draw by London City Lionesses on Sunday.

Frida Maanum fired The Gunners ahead in the 10th minute, but London City Lionesses soon levelled matters at the Emirates Stadium.

Speaking to the media after the match, Arsenal boss Slegers credited the whole squad's effort and dedication despite again being frustrated by a draw on home soil.

"I want [to give] a big shout out to the whole squad because they left absolutely everything on the pitch today," Slegers said. "We came home at 3am from Barcelona that night. We had one day in a managed session to prepare for this game, which is a hard game to play. London City [Lionesses] are a very good team. The players were so dedicated and have done absolutely everything in preparation and on the pitch today. Tribute to the players for me.

"I think the team is in a very good place. A lot of players are performing well. The preparation, the dedication, the hunger for details, they're doing everything they possibly can. It's at a really, really high level."

The Gunners opened the scoring inside the first 10 minutes as Maanum netted in her second consecutive game. Slegers commented on the Norwegian's good form.

She said "Frida was obviously out with a muscle injury. She's back [and] she was really important for us in the game against Barcelona. Two days later, we're here and she played another 90 minutes and scored a great goal. [She] finds really good positions on the pitch again, leading out of possession with her intensity and problem-solving, so she's really important for the team."

The result means that Arsenal remain winless at home in the league this season. Slegers said that while the home form is frustrating, the Emirates Stadium is still a difficult place for opponents.

She said "I think if you look at those first four [games], for example, there are teams that have come here and had a maximum of five shots, and they come away with the goal for some reason. That's been our luck and this one is different, but I don't think we've lost the fear factor. I think it's still a very hard place for the opposition to come here and play."

Commenting on the atmosphere at the Emirates Stadium, Slegers stated that it still very much feels like home for her side.

She said "We love playing at Emirates, it's our home. We had the biggest crowd so far in the season. The atmosphere was fantastic under the lights, the fans were very loud and intense.

"They've been with us. I think Liverpool away was a sell-out, Barca, they were there, and now there are so many here making the effort, being there for us.

"This definitely feels like our home and our place. We love being here. It's been difficult for us to get the three points instead of the one point, and that's very frustrating for ourselves, for the club, for the fans as well."

Arsenal return to action on Thursday evening when they play host to OL Lyonnes in the UEFA Women's Champions League.

articles.title: USMNT's long goodbye to Mauricio Pochettino brings questions about who's next — and who might follow him to Man United
articles.summary: The departing U.S. coach isn't ruling out a reunion with some of his American stars at Old Trafford. Meanwhile, his soon-to-be-former players have some thoug...
articles.body:
CINCINNATI — As Mauricio Pochettino toggles between his last U.S. assignment and his Manchester United mission , the players he's leaving behind are beginning to think about life with a new coach in the near future and whether any of them might join him at Old Trafford.

What characteristics would they like to see in the next leader?

For one, center back Chris Richards said Monday that he hopes the U.S. Soccer Federation hires "somebody who's just as ambitious as Mauricio was. That was one thing: He really came into this federation with a lot of ambition and a lot of goals for not just this team, but also what the future of this team looked like. … We're just looking forward to winning a lot more games, so somebody who comes in and keeps that same culture."

With Pochettino set to coach his 37th and final U.S. match Tuesday (7 p.m. ET, TBS) against Haiti — the second leg of a CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal that's all but been decided after a 6-0 rout Saturday in Miami — USSF officials have begun pivoting to finding a replacement before the March international window.

Chief executive J.T. Batson and chief operating officer Dan Helfrich will lead the search, with women's coach Emma Hayes and assistant sporting director Oguchi Onyewu involved as well. (The USSF hasn't had a sporting director since Matt Crocker left in April.)

In his two-plus years in charge, Pochettino forged a foundation that took a year to take hold but helped propel the U.S. to first place in the World Cup group stage and a Round-of-32 victory before a forgettable defeat. He also welcomed key players in 2025 and introduced a wave of young talent this fall as the U.S. ran off five consecutive victories.

All in all, everyone involved seems to agree the program is in a good place as the 2030 World Cup cycle accelerates.

"When Mauricio came in, he made it very clear it doesn't matter who you are or what you've done for this team already, that your spot is still something you have to earn every camp and every game," midfielder Weston McKennie said. "When the next coach comes in, that's going to be a big thing as well, to not let players get complacent, because playing for the national team is an honor. It's not something that's given."

Pochettino said he hopes the new coach creates the "same link with the players" and "it evolves in the same way that we evolved during the time in that emotional way. … That is my wish, and that's sure going to happen."

As Pochettino said Friday in the news conference announcing his departure, it's uncommon for a coach to depart on such good terms with his employers and players.

"Normally, it's the opposite," he said, with a smile. "You were sacked and you cry because you want to stay."

Pochettino said he would be happy to help the new coach adjust — and he'll be pulling for the U.S.

"My wish and hope is they win and win and win and win," he said. "Because I am not here anymore, I [don't] hope they lose and lose and lose. … Society is more about haters; to say something wrong is not to help. … We want successful people next, and when you are involved and you were treated in the way we were treated, we only wish the very best."

The USSF's search is expected to span the domestic and international markets. Pochettino's assistants, who've been with him for years, are following him to Manchester and aren't in the U.S. mix.

The 54-year-old Argentine said Monday that much of his staff has already reported to Manchester to begin preparing for Sunday's Premier League match at Liverpool. He will report to Manchester on Wednesday.

"When we arrive, it's going to be non-stop," Pochettino said. "We are focused here into finishing in the best way. This is always going to be my team, always going to be my federation until the end. … That is why it's 100 percent now focused here … and then be ready from Wednesday to start to talk about my new club."

Pochettino was the first U.S. hire largely unfamiliar with American soccer since Bora Milutinovic ahead of the 1994 World Cup. (A German, Jurgen Klinsmann, coached the 2014 squad but had lived in the U.S.)

On Monday, Pochettino said players were initially skeptical of an outsider.

"Maybe I didn't feel the support in my head when I arrived," he said, blaming his ego, in part. "'Bahhh, this guy, foreign guy, they came from abroad. What is he going to teach us? … He doesn't know the culture of the American football, soccer.' … But no bad feelings, because I understand they behave in this way."

The next coach will presumably debut in the Nations League semifinals March 25 at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles before preparing for the biennial CONCACAF Gold Cup next summer. 2030 World Cup qualifying will begin no earlier than next fall.

As for Pochettino's final act, tears are sure to flow after genuinely wrestling with his emotions the past week.

"It's going to be a really emotional situation," he said. "It's going to be tough, but now most important is to be focused on the game and try to be very professional because it's important to keep growing like a team, keep evolving."

It's not out of the question a U.S. player or two will join Pochettino in Manchester in the winter transfer window or next summer.

"Good players always have dreams to reach the [highest] level, and United is one of the teams in the [highest] level," he said. "We are going to pay attention in case [United needs] to make some decisions … to players we know really well."

Striker Folarin Balogun, who plans to leave Monaco in French Ligue 1 this winter, could fill a need. So too could McKennie, who has been with Juventus in Italian Serie A for six years.

"He's obviously grown to like this team and seen the quality this team has to offer," McKennie said. "We have a lot of guys due to probably make moves soon, and so it's kind of inevitable [speculation will grow]. … You could potentially see some guys from here being talked about [going] to Man U and potentially it happening."

For the moment, a coach and players will spend a little more quality time together.

"It's going to be a special night for him and for us, but that's football and that's the world of football," McKennie said. "You say goodbyes and new people come in."
